articleTitle: Integrating 3D Printed Microfluidic Channels With Planar Resonator Sensors for Low Cost and Sensitive Liquid Detection
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Planar microwave resonators interact with materials in their vicinity through the electromagnetic field alteration caused by the materials' molecules. In this work, we are presenting 3D printed channels integrated with microwave planar resonators for inline and real-time liquid sensing applications. The designed structure operates at ~ 4.6 GHz with quality factor of 96. The implemented sensor structure provides a low-cost, high yield, inexpensive and robust sensing platform within a thermal operation range of 0 to 90°C. The fabricated sensor demonstrated a distinct difference between sample liquids flowing through the channel and was consistently able to detect an ethanol concentration of 0.4% in water at room temperature. The implemented sensor has footprint of 4×5 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with a short preparation time.

articleTitle: SilicaGel-Integrated Chipless RF Tag for Humidity Sensing
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a new microwave sensor is presented for contactless monitoring of humidity in dry air stream. The platform is based on a pair of passive ring resonators, which are magnetically coupled. The chip-less sensing tag is implemented on a flexible RF substrate and is coupled to the reader resonator, as a result, contactless and highly sensitive sensing has been enabled. The tag integrated within commercial silica gel adsorbent holders to monitor the humidity. The microwave sensor operates at 3.47 GHz including the coupled tag. The noncontact nature of the proposed structure enables humidity monitoring in harsh industrial environment.

articleTitle: Robust Satellite Navigation by Means of a Spherical Cap Conformal Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This contribution presents the design and performance of a dual-band spherical cap adaptive antenna array for safety-critical satellite navigation. The array consists of seven planar elements, flush-mounted in a spherical cap holder. Each element of the array is resonant at dual frequencies with adequate bandwidth to cover the GPS L1/L5 and Galileo E1/E5a/b frequency bands. The interference mitigation and beamforming performance of the array is demonstrated by means of an adaptive beamforming algorithm. The results show a strong potential of the antenna for applications where continuous system availability is essential.

articleTitle: Compact RGW Differential Phase Shifter for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Millimeter wave systems are in a growing need for compact size phased antenna arrays, hence, compact phase shifters, as well. In addition, there are other numerous applications like isolators, filters, and couplers that deploy the phase shifter as an essential component. To implement the proposed phase shifter the Ridge Gap Waveguide (RGW) structure is selected. RGW technology has the advantage of wideband operation over other technologies. Moreover, RGW structures have lower losses and better performance in the millimeter wave band. This work introduces a new RGW structure that deploys ferrite slabs to make a differential phase shifter with very compact size and ultra-flat phase. The proposed non-reciprocal 90° differential phase shifter has less than 10° of phase variations over the operating band.

articleTitle: TDM based Virtual FMCW MIMO Radar Imaging at 79GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper is a demonstration of combining the Time Division Multiplexing (TDM) technique with Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar for range and Angle Of Arrival (AOA) estimation purposes at 79GHz. Using TDM technique, the number of elements of the array can effectively be increased which as a result it enhances the angular resolution. At the end, a 79GHz TDM based FMCW radar is used to show the result of the presented technique on the experimental data.

articleTitle: An RFID Sensor for Early Expiry Detection of Packaged Foods
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: An RFID sensor with the application in the food industry is proposed and investigated. The sensor can be used to evaluate the expiry date of foods. It consists of an RFID tag (the IC and the antenna) and a conductive polymer. The operational mechanism of the proposed sensor is based on the conductivity change of a polymer when it is exposed to the spoiled food. The results show increment of the read range due to decreases of the polymer conductivity at the sensing region influenced by exposure to the rotten food. Consequently, the reader installed at a certain distance can read/detect the RFID signal of a close-to-spoiled food.

articleTitle: Remote Heart Rate Sensing with mm-wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: There are so many patients who need a continuous vital sign monitoring. Monitoring a patient with a wearable device such as using electrode-based electrocardiography (ECG) signal recording device for a long time is very inconvenient. One possible solution is using contactless sensors such as radars to find vital signs of the subjects. In this paper, we demonstrate the use of frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar operating at 77 GHz for monitoring a patient`s heart rate in a retirement environment. Several experiments were conducted to validate the reliability of the radar responses. Finally, the whole system is tested in a bedroom with the radar above a bed and a patient lying on it.

articleTitle: A Novel Algorithm for Wall Characterization in Through the wall Imaging based on Spectral Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Estimation of wall parameters is a critical key for proper through the wall imaging. In this paper, a novel algorithm based on spectral analysis and wall reflection coefficients is presented and shown to be able to accurately estimate the essential parameters of the homogeneous wall. This method just requires S-parameter measurement and proposed formulation makes it useful for any realistic imaging problem. The formulation of the proposed algorithm is discussed along with its application to simulated and measured results

articleTitle: Single-feed Dual-band Aperture-coupled Antenna for 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A single-feed dual-band aperture-coupled antenna for 5G applications is presented. The proposed antenna is designed to operate as a dual-band radiator by utilizing the aperture slot, both as a feed to a microstrip patch at the upper band and a main radiator at the lower band. These two antennas resonate almost independently, and they provide the desired radiation performance at the operating frequency bands; furthermore, the independence of the resonators allows for flexible frequency scaling. The first band (centered at 28 GHz) and the second band (centered at 38 GHz), correspond to the slot aperture and the patch antenna, respectively. The dimensions of the proposed antenna structure are 6 × 6 × 1.27 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The gain, including dielectric and metal losses, is ~ 6.8 dB and 8.25 dB, at 28 GHz and at 38 GHz, respectively. The cross-polarization discrimination is better than 48 dB for both bands.

articleTitle: Active Phased-Array Antennas for Ka/K Mobile Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents the measured results of two sub-arrays for mobile satellite communication systems operating in Ka (Tx) and K (Rx) bands. A 4 × 2 Ka-band (30 GHz) circularly polarized active phased-array antenna is fabricated and tested for different steering angles. Measurements show a high purity right hand circularly polarized (RHCP) radiation pattern over the elevation angle range 0° -±25 ° with axial ratio ≤1.1 dB. Furthermore, a 4 × 1 (20 GHz) dual fed active phased-array antenna is designed and tested. It shows a RHCP radiation pattern with high cross-polarization discrimination ≥27 dB (> 0.7 dB AR) over the elevation range 0° -±25°.

articleTitle: High Gain Wideband Log Periodic Dipole Array Antenna Loaded With Corrugations
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: There is a growing interest in mm-wave antennas and devices for high data transmission to support the future 5G communication. In this work, we have designed a low profile, high gain, broadband four elements printed log periodic dipole array (PLPDA) working over the range of (24-39) Ghz. In the first part of the design, a PLPDA is designed, which achieved around 10.5 dB gain, 49.6% impedance bandwidth. Later some horn corrugation is cascaded to the PLPDA which enhanced the overall gain up to 13 dB, while 52% impedance bandwidth is obtained. All results are validated using two different numerical packages.

articleTitle: A Frequency-Reconfigurable Water-Loaded Planar Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A novel frequency reconfigurable microstrip monopole antenna with a fluidic channel milled on its substrate is proposed. The fluid in the channel modifies the effective permittivity of the dielectric medium and perturbs the E-field distribution in vicinity to antenna arm. The achieved frequency shift is 20.3%, the impedance bandwidth is 28.6% and 32.1% and the peak realized gain is 3.31 dBi and 1.81 dBi when the channel is empty and filled with distilled (DI) water, respectively. Radiation pattern is omnidirectional in both the cases with low cross-polar components.

articleTitle: Complementary Split-Ring Resonators for Non-Invasive Characterization of Biological Tissues
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Planar microwave sensors are very interesting for health applications, such as the investigation of dielectric properties of biological tissues in a non-invasive and contactless manner. In this paper, three structures of complementary split-ring resonators (CSRRs) coupled to microstrip lines are investigated with ex-vivo characterization of animal tissues. Compared to ring resonators, their main advantage consists in more compact sensors, enabling a better local dielectric characterization of the tissues. The extraction of dielectric parameters is obtained by an optimization process based on a comparison of experimental results with electromagnetic simulations with full-wave three-dimensional (3D) finite element method implemented in HFSS and CST.

articleTitle: Antenna Gain and Bandwidth Enhancement Using a Dielectric Superstrate at 60 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Recently, an antenna referred to as fringing field antenna, which is a narrow band in the 60 GHz band. Here, the gain of this antenna is enhanced by broadening the bandwidth and enhancing its gain. A dielectric superstrate is used making a gain enhancement by 4 (i.e., from 11.5 dBi to 15.5 dBi). In addition, 10-dB matching bandwidth is increased from 3.67 % (2.2 GHz) to 7.5 % (4.5 GHz).

articleTitle: End-Launch Horn Antenna Array for Ka-band 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In a large scale antenna system for 5G beamforming, the antenna modules can be designed as end-launch components. This concept is demonstrated by adopting half-height-pin gap waveguide technology to design a 4-element linear array. A quasi-TEM horn antenna is realized by flaring the double ridge that is surrounded by the half-height-pin electromagnetic band gap (EBG) structure. The single antenna element shows an impedance bandwidth (-10 dB) of 35% at 30 GHz with the realized gain of 7 dBi. The same impedance bandwidth is maintained with a 4-element linear array having a gain of 13.6 dBi at 30 GHz. The quasi-TEM double ridge gap waveguide (RGW) antenna is excited through a planar microstrip transition. The microstrip-to-ridge transition is designed and optimized to achieve better impedance match. The overall antenna array performance in the operating frequency range, 27.5~38 GHz, is stable with radiation efficiency around 78 %.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study: Monitoring of Healing Stages of Bone Fracture utilizing UWB Pulsed Radar Technique
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The feasibility study of healing stages after fracture has been performed in this paper. The ultra-wide band (UWB) pulsed radar technique has been applied to monitor the healing stages in the way of numerical approach and simulation study as a proof of concept. The healing stages can be monitored by looking at the changes in amplitude of reflected pulse.

articleTitle: Customized shaped Luneburg Lens Antenna Design by Additive Fabrication
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: —In this paper we present the design and fabrication of modified Luneburg lens antennas. The lens was designed using a quasi-conformal transformation optics approach and fabricated using additive manufacturing. We experimentally validated our methods by designing and fabricating a modified Luneburg lens operating at 24–40 GHz with a beamforming capability of -50° to 50°.

articleTitle: Tissue-Type Imaging for Ultrasound-Prior Microwave Inversion
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper we show results of applying the composite tissue-type imaging method to reconstructions of ultrasound-guided microwave inversions. Structural prior information about the object-of-interest undergoing quantitative microwave imaging is provided to the microwave inversion algorithm via an ultrasound ray-based imaging technique that utilizes a qualitative delay-and-sum method followed by K-means segmentation. The resulting segmented image is utilized as an inhomogeneous numerical background for the microwave finite-element Contrast Source Inversion algorithm. This prior information improves the reconstruction of the complex permittivity. Subsequently, the recently derived composite tissue-type imaging technique, which produces a tissue-type map along with a corresponding probability image, is applied to the reconstructed complex permittivity images.

articleTitle: Fluidically-Tuned Reflection Oscillator at C-Band
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A fluidically-tuned reflection-type oscillator using a substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) resonator is designed and tested. Frequency tuning is achieved by depositing water droplets along the transmission lines that feed the resonator and the oscillator's load matching network. Experimental measurements show that the oscillator can be tuned over a 110 MHz band from 5.053 GHz to 4.943 GHz while its phase noise degrades by 1.2 dB from -125.2 dBc/Hz to -124 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset over the band. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to investigate the fluidic tuning of microwave oscillators.

articleTitle: Dual Polarized Wideband Vivaldi 4x4 Subarray Antenna Aperture for 5G Massive MIMO Panels with Simultaneous Multiple Beams
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband dual linear polarized Vivaldi 4x4 sub-array antenna aperture with low mutual coupling is analyzed for its impedance matching and radiation performance. This antenna also provides good polarization isolation to support simultaneous transmit and receive communications as desired in 5G communications. This array can be used as a base station panel for the Massive Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) array. In addition, Keysight SystemVue tool has been used to generate digital beamforming (DBF) approach based simultaneous multiple beams.

articleTitle: Compact Polarization Diversity Antenna for 28/38 GHz Bands
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, design and analysis of a millimeter wave dual- and dual-polarized antenna for 5G millimeter communications system is presented. The proposed design has a compact structure with size of 5 × 5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. It consists of a rectangular patch with a crossed-slot etched off in the patch to reduce the interference between the two targeted 5G bands of 28 and 38 GHz. To achieve dual polarization performance, the radiating patch is fed by two different 50-Ω microstrip transmission lines. The antenna has -10dB impedance bandwidths of 2.6GHz (26.8-29.4 GHz) and 2.5GHz (37.7-40.2GHz) to cover 28/38 GHz mobile communication bands respectively. The antenna has the merits of miniaturized dimensions, stable broadside radiation patterns with high gains and low cross polarization in both bands of operation.

articleTitle: An Automated System for Measurement of Sensitive Microwave Radiometers
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: An automated system for measuring the sensitivity of microwave radiometers with a free-space input port is described. The Hot/Cold Test Facility (HCTF) exposes a test radiometer to two free-space loads: a hot load formed by ambient-temperature microwave absorber, and to cold sky to act as a cold load. Automation has been added to this facility to improve repeatability, enable long-term studies, and to minimize operator error. We describe the HCTF, discuss measurement errors, and show typical results.

articleTitle: Near-Field Holographic Microwave Imaging Using Data Collected Over Cylindrical Apertures
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In the previously proposed near-field holographic imaging setups, data has been acquired over rectangular apertures. In this paper, a mathematical approach is presented to reconstruct images based on the data acquired over cylindrical apertures. Performance of the proposed technique is studies via simulation. The reconstructed images from the proposed cylindrical data acquisition setup are compared with those of a rectangular setup. It shows superior performance for the former one.

articleTitle: Interferometer based Direction-Of-Arrival Detection System
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents an interferometer-based direction of arrival (DoA) detection system. Unlike conventional six-port based phase discriminators, the proposed architecture uses only three couplers in combination with three receiving antennas. The modeling and analysis of the DoA detection scheme prove that it is possible to improve the measurement accuracy by increasing the inter-element distance between the receiving antennas. The proposed scheme is suitable for use at 5G millimeter wave frequencies as the wavelength is less than one centimeter and many antennas could be easily integrated within the receiver.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Guiding Structure Based on Printed Ridge Gap Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Future communication systems are expected to highly engage in all aspects of the human life. These demanding novel solutions are featured with flexible and wide bandwidth microwave components. In this paper, we introduce a revolutionary solution in microwave guiding structure that can be used to implement reconfigurable microwave components based on printed ridge gap waveguide technology (PRGW). There has been a great interest in PRGW technology as a guiding structure for mm-wave applications as it provides low loss and low dispersion guiding mechanism. A brief study of the proposed technology is presented and illustrated.

articleTitle: A Pattern Diversity Antenna for Ambient RF Energy Harvesting in Multipath Environments
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A pattern diversity antenna configuration is proposed for ambient RF energy harvesting in rich multipath environments. The proposed idea is to combine the radiation patterns of three co-centric dipoles with 60° inter-element angle to cover the entire angular space and increase the harvested energy compared to a single dipole. A realistic design is presented consisting of three offset-fed full-wavelength dipoles printed on a low-cost FR4 substrate. By wounding the dipole arms, the antennas are miniaturized, resulting in an overall small size of the receiver which fits in a circle with a 0.3λ0 diameter at 900 MHz. The performance of the proposed antenna is analyzed by a statistical Monte Carlo approach. It is shown that the proposed antenna, despite having a much smaller form factor compared to a spatial diversity configuration with three dipoles half a wavelength apart, provides the same energy harvesting enhancement.

articleTitle: Space-Time-Varying Surface-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: As of today, the application of space-time modulated media has been limited to parametric amplification, nonreciprocity, and frequency mixing. This article exhibits the functionality of the space-time modulated medium as a surface-wave antenna and demonstrates that a space-time modulated medium makes a perfect antenna. We first present the analytical solution for electromagnetic fields inside a space-time modulated medium. The analytical solution reveals the existence of surface-waves in such a medium as well as their temporal and spatial frequencies. We next introduce the concept of space-time surface-wave antenna system, where the transition of space-wave to surface-wave is utilized for a pure signal receive. The analytical solution is supported by FDTD numerical simulation of the medium, which gives a more in-depth insight into the analysis of the structure. The study is expected to pave the way for further study on the application of space-time media in antenna systems.

articleTitle: Cyber Security Challenges in Autonomous Vehicle: Their Impact on RF Sensor and Wireless Technologies
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) will play a crucial role in nextgeneration and intelligence cars. Autonomous Vehicles (AV) are equipped with the advanced RF and wireless communication and sensor infrastructure for supporting vehicular network. AVs not only help to empower aging populations, but also they provide a powerful, noninvasive, non-threatening modality by which to monitor, interact with, and respond to their passengers' state of being. Ten million AVs or self-driving cars will be on the road by 2020, according to an indepth report recently. Proponents of AVs say that the technology has the potential to benefit society in a range of ways, from boosting economic productivity to reducing urban congestion. However, others including some potential consumers and corporate risk managers have expressed serious concerns over the cybersecurity of the so-called fleet of the future. In this research, we will describe how to develop and implement such functionalities highly secure, trust, reliable and accurate sensors. RF sensors like radars and multitude of other types of RF sensors arrays (IoT based) are an instrumental part of the general sensor configuration required for implementing a robust cyber-security strategy and enhancing privacy in addition to the other autonomous features. There are some challenges and threats such as: : What is a new and important threat in AV and what is the difference between it and the other threat occurred in cyber space? : How can AV be attacked? : What is the difference between security and privacy mechanisms for AV? : Could the risk management be ridable to define, control, and mitigate the risk in an AV? : Could cyber-criminals remotely hijack an autonomous car's electronics with the intention of causing a crash? : Could terrorists command the vehicles similar to the weapons? : Could data stored on-board be unlocked? : Could the AV privacy and passengers be considered? : Is there any secure channel in V2V connection for AV?

articleTitle: Horn and Prism Antenna for Dual Range and Dual FOV Automotive Radar Using 77-GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A novel antenna with a horn array was investigated for a dual range and dual field of view (FOV) automotive radar that uses the 77-GHz band. The structure of the antenna, composed of three types of horn, lens, and prism antennas with different directivities, produces a radiation pattern that had both a narrow FOV at a long-range detection and wide FOV at shortrange detection. A fabricated antenna achieved an antenna gain of 21.5 dBi and a 3-dB beam-width of 22 degrees at boresight and an antenna gain of more than 15 dBi within an angle of ±35 degrees in azimuth. The antenna had a matching band-width of 7 GHz, where the reflection co-efficient, S11, was below -10 dB.

Author Keywords: 77-GHz dual range and dual field of view radar
horn and lens with prism antenna

articleTitle: Modeling of Frequency Shift in RF-MEMS Switches Under Residual Stress Gradient
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Residual stress gradient is unavoidable in thin-film based devices such as radio frequency (RF) micro electro mechanical systems (MEMS) switches. In this paper residual stress gradient is modelled which affect the frequency shift in RF-MEMS switches. Curvature of thinfilms are measured experimentally and then residual stress gradient is modelled analytically and using finite element modeller (FEM). A comparison between analytical model and FEM has been carried out by introducing the initial upward curvature due to residual stress in the model. Beams under residual stress gradient change the pull-in voltage and shows frequency shift which points out that underestimating such effects can lead to inaccurate design and analysis of RF-MEMS switches and subsystems.

articleTitle: Benchmark Diversity Results for Generic Spaced Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: MIMO communication has become a standardized technique but the methodology for designing the required diversity antennas is not yet widely understood. Parameters from models of diversity action are often used by designers without full regard to the inherent assumptions of the models behind the parameters. This paper presents diversity evaluation of a generic dual patch diversity antenna in terms of one widely used parameter, the envelope correlation coefficient (ECC). The calculation of the ECC is undertaken via the inner product of the antenna embedded far-field radiation patterns and circuit coupling parameters (s-parameters). These results can be used to benchmark simulations used in diversity antenna design.

articleTitle: Novel Reconfigurable Antennas using Frequency Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents novel designs of four different W-LAN band pattern reconfigurable antennas. Each of these antennas consists of a dipole as an excitation source of electromagnetic waves (EMW), and an active square frequency selective surface structure (ASFSS). By switching the pin diodes of these screens between ON and OFF, the direction of EMW is controlled, and the omnidirectional radiation pattern that generated by the dipole is converted to a directional beam. As it is essential to design ASFSS with appropriate parameters that meet the design requirements, and to obtain a good beam steering from the proposed antennas, various types of active frequency selective surfaces (AFSS) unit cells are designed. The proposed antennas cover the entire azimuth plane at 5.8 GHz in just four beam-steering steps, where angular beamwidth is achieved in each step.

articleTitle: High Efficiency and Small Antenna With Horn and Lens for 77 GHz Automotive Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: An antenna with a pyramidal horn and a dielectric lens was investigated to reduce a size of long-range automotive radars in the 77-GHz band. By employing an array with two horns and lenses where a diameter of the lens was half of whole output-aperture length, a height of the antenna was reduced while keeping an antenna efficiency high. The fabricated antenna with commercially available materials had the height of 14 mm and achieved the antenna efficiency of 45.6% and a frequency bandwidth of 5 GHz where reflection coefficient S11 was below -10 dB. The antenna had a flat beam whose 3-dB beamwidth was 4.5° in elevation and 15° in azimuth, meaning that the antenna can be used for long range radar with a single beam.

Author Keywords: pyramidal horn and dielectric lens antenna

articleTitle: Printed Ridge Gap Waveguide Rotman Lens for Millimetre-wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: We propose a new beam-forming network (BFN) based on Rotman lens system using printed ridge waveguide technology for millimeter-wave applications. This lens implemented with printed gap waveguide technology for the beam and array ports. A prototype lens is designed with eleven beam ports, sixteen array ports, and eight dummy ports. Using ridge-gap waveguides basis, the proposed lens take place in the air to reduce the loss significantly compared to other designed methods. In addition, an efficient transition to feed beam ports with MS to printed RGW is designed and simulated. The proposed lens is proposed with a multi-layer platform to realize gap waveguide rules and scans over (±40°) angle rang.

articleTitle: Initial Results Using an MLEM-based Reconstruction Algorithm for Breast Microwave Radar Imaging
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Breast microwave imaging (BMI) systems are an emerging breast imaging modality. BMI systems illuminate the breast with a microwave signal and record the scattered field produced by the breast tissues. This work focuses on the development and preliminary validation of a novel reconstruction algorithm for breast microwave radar based on a maximum likelihood expectation maximization (MLEM) algorithm. A correction for the inhomogeneous propagation speed of the microwave signal and for the antennas frequency dependent gain was implemented. Experimental scans of two 3D-printed MRI-based, anthropomorphic breast phantoms were used to validate the algorithm. The MLEM-based algorithm reconstructed images with a contrast between the malignant tumor response and the background clutter greater than 25 dB.

articleTitle: High gain CP Antenna with Low RCS Based on Fabry-Perot Cavity
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The paper proposes a new method for enhancing gain and reducing radar cross section (RCS) a circularly polarized (CP) antenna for applications around 30 GHz, simultaneously. The proposed approach is based on the combination of the FabryPerot cavity (FPC) and polarization conversion surface (PCS) all on a surface. In order to suppress RCS, a reflection phase difference of 180° ±37° between adjacent PCSs is created. The proposed CP antenna with FPC has an impedance bandwidth (23%) ranged from 27 GHz to 34 GHz, peak gain 13.5 dB at 29 GHz with a 7.5 dB gain enhancement. Meanwhile, the proposed structure reduces monostatic RCS bandwidth by more than 35%.

articleTitle: Low Temperature Co-Fired Ceramic Half-Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide Leaky-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A novel leaky-wave antenna implemented in the low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) is presented. Introducing cavities in the structure and removing the conductor planes between tape layers improve radiation efficiency and gain. Moreover, tapering the aperture of the antenna leads to about 10dB reduction of side-lobe level. The antenna has an operating band from 28.3 to 29.1 GHz that is among the proposed 5G frequency bands. The realized peak gain and radiation efficiency of the proposed antenna over the operating band are about 8.5 dB and 80%, respectively. The length, width, and height of the antenna are 40 mm, 16 mm, and 0.5 mm, respectively. The compactness of the antenna and the characteristics of LTCC structure makes it a suitable nominee for modern circuit integration.

articleTitle: Significant Wave Height Estimation without Doppler Spectra
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: For over sixty years [1], the usual procedure to determine the significant wave height from HF-radar data has been to first form the Doppler spectrum from the received radar data, and then process the result to extract important ocean wave parameters, such as the significant wave height, primary wave period, principal wave direction, or even the full directional ocean wave spectrum. In the current work, we bypass the calculation of the Doppler spectrum and still calculate the significant wave height from the received radar data. The new procedure is based on a change-of-coordinates of the expression for the first-order scatter, from which an expression for the wave height in terms of other parameters is obtained directly. The validity of this expression is tested with field data from which a significant correlation with the significant wave height as measured independently by a wave buoy is found.

articleTitle: Flexible Anisotropic Metasurface Transmitarray Unit Cell Design
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A broadband, anisotropic, and linear-polarized transmitarray unit-cell is proposed. Centering the design at 19GHz, four stacked layers of flexible substrate materials achieve a full transmission phase range of 360°. The design shows an independent phase shaping ability for the two orthogonal polarizations. The maximum insertion loss is less than 1.5 dB, considering the different permutations of the unit cell phasing. Full-wave analysis results are presented to elaborate on the proposed potential.

articleTitle: Spectral Smoothing by Multiple Radar Pattern Multiplication for Improved Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a novel technique for improving radar accuracy. In particular, by studying the product of multiple radar beam pattern spectrums from different radar sub-module views, a refined and improved total radar response can be obtained. We examine this radar signal processing approach using a 24GHz frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar system equipped with broadband 1.5GHz substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) antenna arrays to ensure high range resolution. The transmitter is defined by 4 sawtooth signals generated by separated radar sub-modules, each having a multiple input multiple output (MIMO) configuration with 4 receivers at each radar submodule. The measured spectral multiplication of the individual radar sub-modules results in a signal quality improvement of more than 10dB when compared to a MIMO radar configuration with the same architecture.

articleTitle: Complex Permittivity Measurement Based on Planar Microfluidic Resonator Sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a microfluidic sensor is proposed using a microwave planar multiple split-ring resonator (MSRR). The main objective of this real time non-destructive microfluidic sensor is to detect and analyse the dielectric properties of materials using extremely small amount of liquid volumes (2.5μL). The sensing mechanism of the proposed microfluidic sensor is based on frequency shifting and amplitude changing of material under test. An MSRR is employed using a Rogers RT/ Duroid 5880 substrate. Then, a microcapillary made from glass material is loaded on the outer ring slot to observe the perturbation response. The microcapillary is filled with several common solvents and the ideal value of those solvents are used as a reference result. The resonant frequency of the structure with microcapillary is observed to be 2.1 GHz. The functionality and reliability of the proposed sensor are successfully demonstrated through full-wave simulations and measurements. The resonant frequency of the loaded microcapillary showed a shift of 125.5 MHz and 25 MHz when compared to empty microfluidic. Our proposed microfluidic sensor is nondestructive and reliable. Furthermore, it is low cost and fabricated using simple and easy design procedures.

articleTitle: Microwave Near-Field Detection of Single Biological Cells and Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Microwave interferometry techniques provide a means for constructing very sensitive impedance detectors. The impedance approach is well suited to a lab-on-chip based analysis platform as it is label-free and does not require complicated sample preparation. We describe a microfluidic device capable of detecting single biological cells while in flow. The device has a 40zF/√Hz sensitivity. In this paper we show how the approach can be used for detection of mammalian (CHO) cells as well as nanometer scale particles, such as bacteria.

articleTitle: Balanced Corrugated Antipodal Linear Tapered Slot Antenna with Integrated Feeding for Cross- Polarization Suppression
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this work, a balanced Antipodal Linear Tapered Slot Antenna (ALTSA) is proposed and studied with improved cross-polarization performance. This antenna consists of two conventional ALTSAs with one stacked on top of the other, forming a balanced structure. By arranging the middle tapers in the same direction and coinciding with each other, the field components corresponding to the cross-polarization can be canceled, thereby improving the polarization purity. The antenna feeding network from the single layer transmission line to the double layer radiation structure is also presented. Measurement is in good agreement with simulation for both the return loss from 22 to 34 GHz, and the E and H-plane radiation patterns at 28 GHz. The measured antenna gain is 10.32 dBi, and the measured cross-polarization is 28 dB lower than the copolarization. The proposed antenna demonstrates the potential of using balanced structure in the ALTSA design for crosspolarization suppression.

articleTitle: Overview of Fiber Optic Surface Plasmon Resonance Biosensors for Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Fiber Optic Surface Plasmon Resonance (FO-SPR) biosensors are practical miniature sensors that provide real-time monitoring and label-free detection of the concentration of a desired analyte for remote in situ use. These sensors utilize Surface Plasmon Waves (SPWs) excited at a Metal-Dielectric Interface (MDI). In our paper, we explain the background theory of SPWs, operation principle, conventional system design and performance parameters of FO-SPR sensors.

articleTitle: Improving Auroral Clutter Rejection Robustness in Over-the-Horizon Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Robust beamforming is evaluated in an over-the-horizon radar that uses a planar array of monopoles in transmission. Significant auroral clutter rejection improvements are demonstrated with an appropriate choice of diagonal loading.

articleTitle: Wideband Printed Ridge Gap Semi-Log Periodic Structure Antenna for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A wideband semi-log periodic antenna design based on the log periodic antenna is presented. The proposed antenna is fed using a printed ridge gap technology which results in improvement of the efficiency. The proposed design has a matching level less than -10 dB with a fractional bandwidth of 49.37% at 36 GHz. The proposed design has an average realized gain of 6.5 dB over the whole band with stable radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Wideband Reflectarray and Transmitarray Designs Using Polarization Rotating Unit Cells
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: We demonstrate the use of polarization rotating (PR) unit cells in designing wideband reflectarray (RA) and transmitarray (TA) antennas. A reflective/transmissive PR unit cell and its mirror image can provide 1-bit phase quantization over a very wide frequency range. The PR unit cells were used to design a RA and TA antennas, both with aperture dimensions of 30 × 30 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and focal lengths of 30 cm, for operation at X-band. The fabricated RA and TA antenna prototypes provided a maximum realized gain of 24.5 dBi, 3-dB gain bandwidths of up to 40%, and polarization purity and side lobe levels of better than 11.5 dB.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Circularly Polarized Vivaldi Antenna Using Simple Single Layer 2D FSS Polarizer
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a novel wideband polarizer based on a 2D Frequency Selective Surface (FSS), operating in the frequency range of 28 to 32 GHz, is designed and characterized. This polarizer consists of an array of 9 x 9 “T” shaped unit-cells that converts a linearly polarized wave to a circular polarized wave. To demonstrate the principle, the proposed single layer FSS is applied to a linearly polarized Vivaldi antenna operating in the same millimeter-wave frequency band. The simulation results, by placing the proposed polarizer in front of the antenna, show that an axial ratio (AR) smaller than 3 dB is obtained over a wide bandwidth with a gain enhancement, confirming the polarization conversion.

articleTitle: Compact Ultra-Wideband Printed Bandpass Filter Based on Coupled-Line Resonator Loading
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a novel compact design for Ultra-Wideband (UWB) Bandpass Filter (BPF) using a coupled line resonator is proposed. The proposed filter consists of two identical wideband coupling section as input and output stages. In addition, the middle section is loaded with two identical parallel resonators to enhance the out of band rejection by introducing transmission zeros. The proposed filter is implemented using microstrip line technology. The proposed design offers an UWB covering the S, C and G bands used for radar applications starting at 2.5 GHz up to 7 GHz with a matching level exceeding 20 dB. The overall size of the proposed filter is shorter than a half wavelength at the center frequency. The design procedure as well as the final results of the proposed design are illustrated based on two different numerical solutions for outcomes validation.

articleTitle: A Compact Uniplanar Tri-band Antenna for Wearable Smart Watches
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a uniplanar tri-band antenna for smart watch applications is presented. Implemented on a FR4 substrate and occupying 38× 38 × 0. 8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, the antenna supports Bluetooth, WiFi 2.4/5. 8 GHz and WiMAX 3. 8 GHz bands. The antenna is composed of an edge tapered, bent monopole element with a capacitively coupled inverted L shorting strip supporting the triband operation in 3:1 VSWR standard and exhibiting positive gain in all bands. The specific absorption rate of the antenna is well within the acceptable limits specified by FCC.

articleTitle: Lumped Element Model of a Transdirectional Coupled Line Coupler
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Transdirectional coupled line couplers have gained a lot of attention due to their isolation between the input and output ports as compared with other traditional directional couplers. A novel fully lumped element model for the transdirectional coupler with generic equations for a given coupling coefficient is presented. Capacitors are used to represent the coupling mechanism between the two coupled lines. A lumped element transdirectional coupler design with 3 dB coupling will be presented and results given.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Folded-Shorted Patch Antenna for Military Search and Rescue Operations and Emergency Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: There has been a gradual increase in wearable-based applications such as Nike plus, Google glass, Fitbit and smart watches to name a few. In this paper, a dual-band compact folded-shorted patch (FSP) antenna is developed and is operational at 400 MHz and 2.4 GHz for UHF satellite communications and WBAN/WLAN technologies, respectively. Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) is used as a flexible substrate for the FSP antenna making it suitable for wearable applications. Moreover, the compactness and durability of this antenna make it appropriate for military search and rescue operations and emergency communications, and the presence of the PDMS substrate makes it resilient to harsh environmental conditions while also providing flexibility for the user.

articleTitle: Fully Printed VO2 Switch Based Reconfigurable PIFA / T-shaped Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A recent trend in frequency reconfigurable antennas is the use of a vanadium dioxide (VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) layer as a radiofrequency switch to operate at different frequency bands. Typically, the deposition of a VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> switch utilizes complex fabrication processes which result in higher costs. The ideal approach would be to use low-cost additive manufacturing techniques, such as screen printing. This work presents a novel fully screen-printed frequency reconfigurable PIFA / T-shaped monopole antenna with a printed VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> switch. The switch operates through thermal activation and reconfigures the frequency band. The antenna operates at 2.7 GHz band or at 3.5 GHz band for two different operational modes of the VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> switch. The antenna achieved 2.14 dBi gain at 3.5GHz.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized RGW Slot Antenna Fed by Ferrite Based Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Ridge Gap Waveguide (RGW) technology is a promising technology, especially for the millimeter wave bands. Hence, the need for antennas utilizing the same technology is growing fast to provide complete solutions to the applications in the millimeter wave band. Both linear polarization and circular polarization are deployed in the communication systems depending on the required system needs. Antennas with circular polarization have a remarkable advantage over the linear antennas since they overcome the polarization mismatching and misalignment problems. Here, a circularly polarized antenna that deploys a compact ferrite based differential phase shifter is introduced. The proposed antenna has an impedance matching bandwidth of 16.67% at 30 GHz with a 3 dB axial ratio. Simulations are obtained by two numerical packages, where both results have an excellent agreement with each other.

articleTitle: Frequency Reconfigurable Implant Antenna for MICS and ISM Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Frequency reconfigurable compact antenna is presented in this paper for biomedical implant applications. Switching between two frequency bands of Medical Implant Communications Services (402-405 MHz) and Industrial Scientific and Medical (902-928 MHz) bands are realized by using PIN diodes. The overall size of the antenna element is compact with dimensions of 15 × 12 × 0.635 mm. Two radiating element configuration of spiral and monopole are embedded in the top layer of substrate Rogers RT6010 for the radiations in the MICS and ISM frequency bands. The proposed antenna is analyzed and optimized in CST for various dimensions of spiral segments, monopole and coplanar waveguide ground plane. The frequency response for the two states of the proposed antenna along with radiation plots are presented for verification of the concept.

articleTitle: Analysis of Slot Loading in Elliptical Patch- A Characteristic Mode Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Perturbation of the geometry through a narrow slot has been studied for an elliptical microstrip patch antenna. The loading effects have been studied from modal perspective. The slot is found to suppress the nearest orthogonal mode. As a consequence, the cross-polarized radiation is also reduced. Thus the modal analysis can provide a systematic guideline for enhancing the polarization purity of a desired mode.

articleTitle: Wideband Cavity-Backed Spiral Antenna Design and Mutual Coupling Study in A Closely-Spaced Array
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper deals, first, with the design of a 6 to 18GHz Cavity Backed Archimedean Spiral Antenna (CB-ASA) whose performance, in terms of VSWR, gain, and axial ratio, was improved by utilizing multiple absorbing materials. Then, by placing two spiral elements side-by-side, the mutual coupling effect was investigated in a two-element CB-ASA array, in which one element was excited while the other was passive with a matched load. The results show little effect on the performance of the active element due to the mutual coupling with the adjacent element, with less than 3dB axial ratio, less than 2 dB VSWR and consistent radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Applications of SAR Remote Sensing in the Arctic: A Review
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: We give an overview of some of the applications of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) remote sensing in the Arctic regions. The review places special emphasis on the potential of high resolution SAR to provide quantitative insights - day and night at nearly all-weather conditions - into the physical properties, at meter-scale spatial resolution, of soils (e.g., soil moisture, roughness, and climate-induced permafrost displacements), sea-ice (e.g., ice type, distribution, and motion) and snowpack volumes (e.g., snow cover area, density, and snow water equivalent).

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of Colinear Antenna-Array Using a Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a new band-stop frequency selective surface is presented to convert omnidirectional pattern to directional pattern and enhance the antenna gain. The designed FSS unit-cell is composed of a Jerusalem cross shape strip at the top and a square ring strip at the bottom and holds a size of 0.46λ × 0.46λ (at 28 GHz). The performance of the structure is optimized using CST microwave studio. In this structure, an FSS layer is employed with an array of 3 × 4 of unit cells and is located in the vicinity of an omnidirectional colinear antenna array as a radiating source, which is designed to resonate at 28 GHz. Obtained results show a gain enhancement of 2.8 dBi compared with the unloaded case at 28 GHz. In addition, the reflection coefficient remained under -10 dB across its frequency band.

articleTitle: Impact of Inkjet and 3D Printing Methods on Low Weight and Complex Structure Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, impact of the inkjet and 3D printing methods on design and development of the novel antennas and arrays is discussed. Both techniques have got great attention in the recent years and are going to receive further importance as we move towards the 5G technology era. Some examples of inkjet and 3D printed antennas being carried out in the Antenna and Microwave Lab (AML) at San Diego State University will be discussed. The author had an opportunity to learn antennas while working with Prof. Lot Shafai at the University Of Manitoba. This provided the author a very high impact antenna engineering hands-on-training and which has contributed to his profession and in educating several other antenna engineers.

articleTitle: Next generation vehicular communications via interworking of DSRC and TV White Space
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this work, we propose the use of TV White Space (TVWS) to complement the operation of DSRC technology in vehicular environments, as a Next Generation Mobile Communications platform for vehicular networking. When a DSRC channel is highly congested due to an increased vehicular density or network traffic, a TVWS network could be used as an off-loading option to meet the strict delay required for applications, in particular for emergency messages dissemination. We compare the behavior of a DSRC network and a TVWS network for the case of V2V communications, when emergency messages need to be disseminated in urban and suburban environments. We take into consideration realistic signal propagation models for each network, the distance between vehicles, and the minimum number of hops required when a multi-hop dissemination mechanism is used. We show that the delay using TVWS is less than the delay using DSRC in NLOS urban and suburban scenarios, making TVWS a good candidate for message dissemination when the main network cannot guarantee message delivery.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave High Gain Printed Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper investigates the effect of substrate surface-waves on the radiation characteristics of a printed monopole at 60 GHz. The use of metallic sheets, dielectric slabs, and EBG structures is investigated in order to control the surface-waves and their effect on the gain and radiation characteristics of the printed monopole.

articleTitle: Design of High-Gain Ka-Band Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna excited by Printed Ridge Gap Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents the design of Antipodal Vivaldi antenna (AVA) excited by a low-loss waveguiding structure commonly known as printed ridge gap waveguide (PRGW). The simulated result shows the designed antenna has wide impedance matching and an average gain of 13.5 (±1) dBi after dielectric loading over Ka-band.

articleTitle: Measurements of Composite Reflectors across Q-Band (33–50 GHz) and W-Band (75–115 GHz)
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: We present measured reflectivity of mirrors made of carbon fibre composite materials across Q-Band (33-50 GHz) and W-Band (75-115 GHz). High reflectivity is demonstrated and indicates that these composite reflectors are suitable for low-noise radio telescopes.

articleTitle: Variability in Clinical Data Obtained with Flexible Time-Domain Radiofrequency Breast Monitor
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This work reports initial results of an extensive clinical trial of a microwave-range, conformal prototype for breast health monitoring. The clinical data was recorded with a multistatic time-domain radiofrequency radar on volunteering patients whose mammogram or MRI had previously indicated an abnormality. Before the results are processed using a range of techniques, data is analyzed for variability. In this study, we investigate the number of signals which exceed a prescribed threshold in terms of peak voltage. We assess whether those below the threshold are associated consistently with certain transreceiving antenna pairs. Such analysis with raw recorded signals can help us optimize antenna placement in future versions of the prototype system.

articleTitle: End-Fire Substrate Integrated Waveguide Beam-Forming System for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents the simulated and measured results of a substrate integrated beam-forming network that combines the steering capabilities of a 4×4 Butler matrix and the horizontal polarization of a corrugated Vivaldi antenna array for 5G end-fire applications. The system demonstrates a ± 25° sweep of the main beams as well as a gain that ranges between 8.7 dB and 11.7 dB at a center frequency of 25 GHz. Good agreement between experimental and simulated results validates the design approach.

articleTitle: SAR Imaging for a 79GHz FMCW Radar Based on MUSIC Method
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: We present a 2D Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging problem for Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radars. We use the Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) method in the structure of Range Migration Algorithm (RMA) to obtain a high resolution image compared to the case of using Fourier transform. We then use experimental data gathered from a 79GHz FMCW radar to demonstrate the ability of the proposed technique to produce a 2D high resolution focused image.

articleTitle: An Inexpensive Ultrawideband Radar for High-Resolution Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents an inexpensive custom designed ultrawideband (UWB) radar for high-resolution applications. The transmitted signal is a mono-pulse with 110ps pulse-width and 6Vp-p amplitude. The UWB receiver is developed based on the time expansion method. A strobe pulse, with 85ps pulse-width, is used to sample the periodic RF pulse train at a series of offsets during successive periods. An expansion factor is defined based on the difference in pulse repetition frequencies of the strobe and RF pulses. The expanded reconstructed pulse spectrum is scaled-down according to this factor. The designed portable UWB radar system is suitable for biomedical or industrial applications with high-resolution demands.

Author Keywords: high-resolution remote sensing and imaging applications

articleTitle: Full-Wave Analysis and Design of a Wideband GaAs pHEMT MMIC LNA
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a wideband monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) low noise amplifier (LNA) using GaAs pseudomorphic high electron mobility transistor (pHEMT) technology. The flat gain of 30 dB ± 0.5 dB is achieved using a three-stage amplifier topology over 412 GHz. The minimum noise figure of 1.0 dB is achieved in a packaging chassis within the frequency band. In order to achieve such a low noise over a wideband, several bandwidth enhancement techniques are applied in the design. An inductive feedback at the source of the first stage results in a very wideband input matching (|S11| <; -12 dB) over 3-15 GHz. The gold wire bonds at the input and output of the chip are separately analyzed and modeled into matching networks to ensure wideband low noise behavior of the chip after packaging. This GaAs pHEMT LNA is suitable for radio astronomy receivers such as the Atacama Large Millimeter Array Band 3 IF warm amplifiers.

articleTitle: Cryo-CMOS Low-Noise Amplifier for the Square Kilometre Array
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents early results from the investigation of a cryogenically cooled CMOS (Cryo-CMOS) low-noise amplifier (LNA). The LNA was designed in a bulk 65-nm CMOS process. Measurements were performed at 300 K and a noise temperature (figure) of 12 K (0.18 dB) was achieved at 1420 MHz (the neutral hydrogen line). The amplifier also exhibits $\mathrm {a}32 \pm 1.65$ dB gain, an input return loss better than 8.3 dB, an output return loss better than 15.6 dB and consumes a total of 105 mW, 51 mA from a 0.7-V supply and 69 mA from a 1-V supply. From simulations, the LNA is expected to achieve a noise temperature (figure) of 4.5 K (0.07 dB) at an ambient temperature of 77 K while consuming 35 mW, 22mA from a 1-V supply and 19 mA from a 0.7-V supply.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Antenna Based on Printed Ridge Gap Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The rapid development of wireless mobile communication systems is highly affected by the availability of innovative antenna technologies such as reconfigurable antennas. In this paper, the reconfiguration feature is implemented based on a novel concept, namely, reconfigurable printed ridge gap waveguide technology (RPRGW). This technology will enable the implementation of reconfigurable microwave components that needed for the construction of robust and adaptable communication systems. A reconfigurable patch antenna is designed based on this technology. The simulation results show that a frequency-reconfigurable patch antenna can be achieved using the proposed revolutionary configuration.

articleTitle: Multi-Plane Magnetic Near-Field Data Inversion Using the Source Reconstruction Method
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: We deal with a specific planar near-field measurement system where magnetic field data is collected by a compact 2-D array of magnetic probes. To enable this planar system to utilize a more complete set of magnetic field data, we present a method that can invert multiple planes of magnetic data collected by rotating the antenna under test. It is then synthetically shown that by using the presented method the far-field accuracy of an inset-fed patch antenna can be improved compared to the original case where only one plane of magnetic data is utilized.

articleTitle: Regularization Approaches for a Non-Iterative Eigenfunction-Based Electromagnetic Inversion Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Several options for regularizing a novel non-iterative eigenfunction-based inverse-source solver related to 2D Electromagnetic Imaging are presented. Regularization is implemented in the form of constraint equations that use the fact that all contrast sources outside the imaging domain are zero. The different options are evaluated via their improved imaging performance on a few examples based on synthetically derived forward data. It will be shown that the proper selection of constraint equations can significantly enhance the performance of this non-iterative algorithm.

articleTitle: D-Band Compact and High Gain Pyramid Dielectric Antenna Array Using Silicon Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents an array of two Frustum Pyramid dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) based on a coplanar-waveguide (CPW) fed for D-band millimeter-wave application. The DRA takes the shape of a truncated apex pyramid. Fabrication of the Pyramid DRA is a two mask process. The fabrication process includes wet etching of high resistivity Si wafer using KOH solution along the crystalline surfaces to fabricate the pyramid like shape. The second mask is used to define the CPW feed network on the backside of the antenna. The compact-size and low profile of the Pyramid DRA make it great candidate for short-range wireless communication and high-resolution imaging. The simulation of the antenna array in the D-band shows a gain of 12.24dB and 82% radiation efficiency at 176 GHz.

articleTitle: Breast Imaging with Multiphysics Prior for Improved Tumour Detection and Localization
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, we present a method of combining multiphysics prior information extracted from ultrasound and microwaves to enhance tumour detection and localization. First, a low frequency ultrasound modality is used to extract high resolution structural information of the breast. This information serves as prior information to improve dielectric property estimates using microwave inversion based imaging method. The quantitative breast properties estimated from microwave inversion provide additional useful prior information that can be used with microwave radar based approach for improved target localization. The method is simulated using 2D realistic breast model with two embedded tumours and the results demonstrate desired enhancements.

articleTitle: Arbitrarily Polarized Antennas Based on Periodic Media with Tilted Axis of Periodicity
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The polarization of an antenna can be controlled by the field existing in its feeding waveguide. The concept and design methodology of a special feeding mechanism to control the polarization of millimeter wave antennas is presented. With a single input source and without any change in the antenna dimensions itself, the polarization of the radiated field can be controlled and altered to take any general state with any required axial ratio. An expression for the axial ratio is derived analytically and given as a function of the design parameters.

articleTitle: Surface Reactance on a Periodic Modulated Thickness Grounded Slab
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A modulated reactance is useful for realizing leaky-wave antennas. A grounded dielectric slab with thickness modulation is used to obtain a modulated reactance. The problem of a thickness-modulated slab is simplified by studying a constant-thickness grounded slab with an air gap between the physical structure and field points (where the impedance is evaluated). The surface reactance of a line source excited grounded slab is analyzed. Numerical evaluation of a Sommerfeld integral in the w plane is used to evaluate the fields near the source region. It is shown that near the source the reactance is not constant. Away from the source, an asymptotic approximation is used to evaluate the reactance. This allows a simplified synthesis procedure whereby the air gaps above the thickness-modulated slab can be ignored. The sinusoidal and square-wave impedance profiles are validated against a thickness-modulated slab using a commercial full-wave solver (CST).

articleTitle: Via Staggering Loss in Substrate Integrated Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The loss contributions of a Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) with staggered vias is investigated and quantified using precision simulations. Besides choosing an appropriate substrate material and cladding smoothness, the main design factor to reduce SIW loss is to increase the substrate thickness. As the substrate thickness increases, the requirements for manufacturability force the use of larger diameter vias, which forces the staggering of the SIW via-wall to reduce the side-wall leakage. The gaps in the staggered vias degrades the purity of the TE <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> mode causing additional loss at discrete frequencies. Being cognisant of these effects fosters improved SIW design, including configuration and materials usage.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement Techniques for mm-Wave On-Chip Antennas on Lossy CMOS Platforms
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: With the advent of number of applications in the mm-wave bands, antenna sizes are becoming small enough to fit them on mm-scale Integrated Circuits (ICs), commonly known as microchips. Integration of antenna on a chip along with the driving circuits in the standard CMOS process can enable a true RF System-on-Chip (SoC) solution, however, Silicon used in CMOS is very lossy and has a high dielectric constant. This results in low gain and efficiency antennas which also suffer from surface waves issues at mm-wave frequencies. In this paper, we will present Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) surface to increase the gain/efficiency of the on-chip antenna realized in standard CMOS platforms. The gain and radiation efficiency of 1.7dBi and 42.52% are achieved respectively.

articleTitle: A Flexible Printed Complementary Split-Ring Resonator Based Chipless RFID
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A fully inkjet-printed flexible chipless RFID is presented in this paper. It consists of a regular microstrip transmission line on the top plane that is coupled with two back “etched” slit-ring resonators called complementary split-ring resonators (CSRR) on the ground plane. The CSRRs resonate at around 2.3 GHz and 3.4 GHz, respectively. The design is characterized in both simulations (ANSYS HFSS) and experiments. The future application of this RFID will focus on sensing where one resonator will be utilized as the sensor, and another one will be used as the reference.

articleTitle: A Log-Periodic Monopole Array with Uniform Spacing
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a log-periodic monopole array antenna with end-fire radiation and vertical polarization. It consists of 13 monopole elements and a meandering microstrip line on the bottom as the feeding line. The adjacent monopoles are of uniform spacing instead of conventional logarithmic spacing. A prototype is fabricated and tested. Measured results show that an impedance bandwidth from 2 to 6 GHz (3:1) for VSWR <;2 and a realized gain better than 7.6 dBi over the same operating frequency band are obtained.

articleTitle: Efficient Reflective Polarization Rotator in Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The paper proposes an efficient and wideband polarization rotator composed of two-layer surfaces for millimeter wave applications. The simulations show that polarization conversion ratio (PCR) is completely efficient and higher than 95% for both polarizations (x and y) normally incident EM waves so that the bandwidth is ranged from 19 GHz to 49 GHz, equivalent to 88% relative bandwidth. The mechanism for linearly polarization rotation is described by decomposed electric field components that couple with different resonance modes of the structure. Besides, the surfaces are approximately robust under the incident oblique angles. The suggested structure with the excellent efficiency of polarization conversion has various potential applications in different areas such as imaging, modern communications, and new polarization-control devices.

articleTitle: Wideband Electrically Small Antenna Internally Loaded With Non-Foster Circuit
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a wideband electrically small antenna using internally loaded Non-Foster circuit. The negative capacitance provided by the circuit can significantly compensate the high reactance of the antenna and match it in a wide bandwidth. However in order to accurately predict the behaviour of the active antenna, the EM model of the non-foster circuit is taken into account in the full wave simulation of the antenna. The loaded antenna having an electrical size ka = 0.3 is matched in a wideband (34%).

articleTitle: Characteristic Mode Analysis of a Vertical Dipole Above Lossy Dielectric Half-space
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel formulation for determining the characteristic modes of a vertical electric dipole aligned in dielectric half-space. Complex image techniques have been employed to determine the corresponding field integral equation. The modal perturbation due to the dielectric ground has been compared with various heights for better physical understanding.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Antenna Design for Portable Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A reconfigurable patch antenna design for portable applications is presented in this paper. The antenna consists of patch lines connected in Tree shape on front side and the back side contains a T and L-shaped strips which are shorted with patch on front side for increasing electrical length. Frequency reconfigurablility is achieved by inserting three RF PIN diodes at suitable locations. This antenna is reconfigurable among different frequencies including GSM 900 and LTE bands such as 1.4 GHz, 1.6 GHz, 1.7 GHz, 2.5 GHz, and 2.6 GHz. Antenna is simulated in CST and a prototype is fabricated to compare measured results with simulated results.

articleTitle: In Situ Passive Microwave and UAV Observations of Early Summer Sea Ice
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This research focuses on comparing the passive microwave brightness temperature signatures of open water and melted sea ice floe surface types over a series of frequencies, polarizations and incidence angles. A surface-based radiometer was used to collect microwave emissions for 19-, 37-and 89-GHz frequencies at both horizontal and vertical polarizations for melt pond laden ice floes and open ocean, along with unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) surveys of each scanned floe. Brightness temperatures were compared for each surface type, noting the locations of ice floe melt ponds within the footprint. Analysis showed that 37 GHz H experienced the greatest sensitivity and 89 GHz V experienced the least sensitivity to melt pond presence on ice floe surfaces.

articleTitle: Radar Cross Section Based Passive Wireless Sensor for Volatile Sensing
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a radar cross section-based passive, wireless acidic/basic volatile sensor with a built-in reference enabling differential sensing capabilities. The concept of a two-electrode gas sensing scheme coupled with indirect capacitive transduction is shown. The low cost, passive nature and volatile sensing ability makes the sensor suitable for food quality monitoring applications. Simulation results and preliminary measurements of the proposed sensing element are presented. Simulations indicate a sensitivity of 188MHz change in resonant frequency for 1pF change in capacitance.

articleTitle: Electronically Tunable Transmission Zeros Bandpass Filter with Notch Response
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a design of tunable transmission zeros bandpass filter with a notched response in a single device.
