The bandpass filter is designed using 7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order short circuited stub filter. Then, the first short circuited stub is replaced with two sections of open circuited stub to exhibit the transmission zeros at lower/higher stopband. The varactor diode is placed at the J-shape open circuited stub to produce tunable transmission zeros by tuning the voltage on the varactor diodes with range from 0 V to 6 V. The U-shape notched response produced high selectivity and attenuation at resonant frequency of 5.2 GHz. The fabricated result shows good agreement with the simulated results. This type of filter is very useful for applications where the undesired signals and interference will be eliminated within the passband response such as medical electronic, radar and 5G applications.

articleTitle: Terahertz Field Localization Using Slot Dielectric Waveguide Implemented in Silicon-On-Glass (SOG) Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Slot dielectric waveguide implemented in Si-OnGlass (SOG) technology is presented for field localization at the THz frequency range. The waveguide characteristics are studied using simulations. Moreover, waveguide dimensions are optimized to maximize the field localization. The presented structure can be a platform for highly sensitive THz sensors and high performance THz nonlinear devices.

articleTitle: Air Quality Monitoring Using UWB Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Carbon nanotubes (CNT) have exceptional electrical properties that make them likely candidates for Iow cost wireless gas sensors. In this work, we present a novel design scheme for a low-cost ammonia gas sensor utilizing an UWB radar operating in the 3-10 GHz range. When exposed to gas, significant changes in the amplitudes of the backscattered signals of the CNT films are observed. Coupling of a CNT-based passive sensor with the radar enables remote gas detection with high selectivity, at a considerably lower cost in comparison to most commercially available gas sensors.

articleTitle: Glucose Concentration Estimation using Electromagnetic Waves
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The feasibility research of estimating glucose concentration using mm-wave has been performed in this paper. The real based blood with different glucose concentration has been realized and validated with a commercial glucometer. The signal processing has been applied to the measured raw data to correlate the glucose concentration. The correlation we obtained has demonstrated that the glucose concentration can be inversely inferred using an interpolated line.

articleTitle: Multi-functional, Active and Information Processing Antenna Surfaces in Chip-scale THz Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Silicon-based integrated circuit technology provides a great platform for enabling compact, efficient, low-power, chip-scale THz systems for new applications in sensing, imaging and communication While this is partially facilitated by scaling that has pushed device cut-off frequencies (f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub>, f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub>) up into the sub-THz and THz frequency range, the true paradigm shift in silicon integration is that it provides a unique opportunity to enable a new field of active THz electromagnetics realizable through a circuits-EM-systems co-design approach. At these frequencies, the chip dimension is several times larger than the THz wavelengths which allows novel scattering and radiating properties in a substrate that simultaneously supports a billion high-frequency transistors that can generate, process and sense these signals. The ability to actively synthesize, manipulate and sense THz EM fields at subwavelength scales with circuits opens up a new design space for THz electronics. THz architectures emerging from this space are often multi-functional, reconfigurable and break many of the classical trade-offs of a partitioned design approach. This paper provides examples to illustrate this design methodology on THz signal generation with beam-forming and spectrum control and THz spectrum sensing.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Shared-Aperture Slot Array Design Concept
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A shared-aperture design concept is presented for a dual-band array where the ratio of the frequencies is flexible. At the lower frequency, the array is dual-polarized and the elements are cavity-backed crossed slots. The height of the cavity is reduced by adopting an “inverted T” configuration. For the higher frequency, single-polarized slot subarrays are fitted between the crossed slots, and use ridged waveguide for high aperture efficiency. The all-metal design is inherently robust and its sandwich-like structure suits different fabrication techniques. The applications for this kind of antenna include both terrestrial and space-borne missions, particularly synthetic aperture arrays.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave High-Gain Ridge Gap Beam Steerable Antenna for 5G wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A novel high-gain beam steerable antenna is presented to rotate the radiation pattern continuously around the broadside axis at 60 GHz frequency band. A broadside nulled pattern patch antenna is designed with ridge gap waveguide (RGW). A phase gradient metasurface (PGM) is implemented on top of the antenna which by mechanically rotating the PGM surface around its center, the radiation pattern can be rotated continuously. The proposed PGM surface behaves like a soft surface, and consists of square-shaped unit cells placed on the host substrate with a relative permittivity of 3.

articleTitle: High-order unconditionally stable time-domain finite element method
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach for time-domain finite element (FETD) electromagnetic analysis. The new method combines the property of high-order approximation in the time-domain with the crucial property of unconditional stability. The proposed method has been used in circuit simulation, and relies on employing a specific formulation of the numerical inversion of the Laplace transform. The method has been validated using one dimensional scattering from a dielectric object.

articleTitle: Comparative Experimental Radar Target Characterization Data Using Spatial and Transient Singularity Expansion Methods
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, we consider a new approach for radar target characterization using the recently-proposed spatial singularity expansion method (S-SEM) and compare it with traditional temporal (transient) singularity expansion method (T-SEM). This study is performed by analyzing measured time-domain radiated field and the frequency-domain antenna current Green's function (ACGF) of a thin-wire antenna, respectively. The objective here is to compare the complex poles of the two approaches using simulation and measurement verification. Also, we anticipate that this preliminary study will facilitate developing a general mathematical formulation of the relation between spatial and transient SEMs, which remains an open problem.

articleTitle: Ka-band modulated metasurface antennas fabricated by metal additive manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Metasurface (MTS) antennas present an equivalent modulated reactance tensor in the aperture plane, which is designed to gradually radiate a surface-wave (SW). The modulation results in the (-1) indexed Floquet mode entering the visible region, thus becoming a leaky-wave (LW) mode with curvilinear phase-contour. In this paper, we explore the use of metallic MTSs to synthesize the reactance tensor required to obtain an objective radiation pattern, with a given shape and polarization. The proposed structure is particularly well suited to fabrication by metal additive manufacturing. We have designed several metallic MTS antennas, verifying their performance by full-wave simulations. We have also fabricated a prototype, and the measurements have validated the simulation results.

articleTitle: Overview of 3-D Printed Substrates for Enhanced Microstrip Patch Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the different uses of additive manufacturing of substrates to enhance the performance of microstrip patch antenna design. Innovations with the substrates using 3-D printing is reported to result in wider bandwidths, higher gains, and in some cases substrate flexibility and performance stability with substrate curvature.

articleTitle: Reflecto-Transmittive Antenna using Active Frequency Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A novel reflecto-transmittive antenna is presented using active frequency selective surface (AFSS). The reflecto-transmittive screens are shaped resembling to parabolic reflector. The structure consists of an AFSS array, and a patch antenna used a feed. Each element in the array contains of two rectangular shaped patches connected with each other by a high-frequency pin-diode. By switching the diode between ON and OFF states, the reflection and transmission characteristics of the element are controlled. Three AFSS panels are used to investigate the potential of the antenna in reflecting and transmitting the radiation beams. To shape the proposed antenna with parabolic reflector, two panels beside the central are rotated to various angles. The proposed antenna results in maximum directivity of 11.9 dBi for ON state (reflection), while a 7.8 dBi for OFF state (transmission). The maximum directivity is achieved when 15 ô rotation angle is applied to side AFSS panels towards the feed. The antenna performance is evaluated at 2.45 GHz. The performance of the proposed antenna is compared with an antenna designed with PEC in the same environment. The obtained results show a good agreement.

articleTitle: Active Phasers based on Co-directional Couplers for Millimeter-wave Analog Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: An active phaser based on co-directional couplers is proposed for achieving a flat magnitude transmission while preserving its strong dispersive delay response. The phasers are realized using Half-Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide (HMSIW) structures, and are successfully demonstrated using full-wave simulations. Due to the non-TEM nature of the device, the proposed phasers are ideally suitable for mm-wave real-time analog signal processing systems.

articleTitle: ANTEM 2018 Subject Index Page
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Contains an entry for each technical presentation included in this conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Element Around a Thin Cylinder
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The design analysis for a cylindrical conformal PIFA antenna for mounting on a thin conducting cylinder is presented. The thin cylinder means that standard groundplane principles do not apply for antenna design, and that the antenna configurations must be evaluated numerically. The.. factor and fractional bandwidths are used here to guide the design. This antenna has good potential for electrically thin cylindrical structures such as found on unmanned aerial vehicles, drones, bicycles, and some radio masts.

articleTitle: Broadband CP SIW-Integrated DRA Array with Wideband Axial-Ratio for Millimeter-Wave System Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a Ka-band circularly polarized dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) array antenna fed by substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) is presented. The 2×2 circularly polarized L-shaped DRA elements are employed as the radiating elements. The sequential rotation technique is introduced to realize wideband circular polarized characteristics. The proposed antenna structure is symmetric, low loss and compact. The simulated results show that the proposed 2×2 array has a 3-dB large aerial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 15.8 % from 33.1 GHz to 38.8 GHz with an average CP gain of 8.5 dBi. Symmetric radiation pattern with low cross-polarization of 21 dB is obtained.

articleTitle: Utilizing Spherical Near-Field Measurement Data in Antenna On-Platform Performance Studies
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Spherical near-field (SNF) measurement techniques have become the preferred approach for antenna testing. This paper argues in favour of importing detailed measured pattern data obtained from such testing into the on-platform (and other) modelling of these antennas when in situ performance is required. Two representative examples are given.

articleTitle: 4x4 Dual-band Circular Polarized antenna array for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A dual band circular polarized antenna array for millimeter wave applications is proposed. The 4x4 array consists of rectangular loop elements with mirror image printed on both sides of substrate. The proposed design is proving more than 19 dBi gain at 28GHz and 38 GHz bands. Moreover, this antenna array covers 3 GHz bandwidth at 28GHz and 1.7 GHz for 38 GHz band. Furthermore, the low-cost proposed array is providing Circular polarization in both frequency bands with axial ratio less than 3 dB.

articleTitle: A Multi-Bias Correlated Parameter Extraction Method for Microwave Transistor Modeling
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper proposes a new multi-bias correlated parameter extraction method for microwave transistor modeling. The initial small-signal equivalent circuit element values are extracted using an analytical method. Optimum element values are obtained using a gradient optimizer by including multiple sets of different DC bias models in one fitting process. The validity of the developed modeling approach has been verified by the good agreement and less than 2% deviation between the simulated and measured results for different sizes of gallium nitride transistors over a wide range of DC bias conditions and broad frequency range.

articleTitle: Design of a Flexible Broadband RHCP/LHCP Polarizer Unit-Cell
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A broadband, flexible and quad-layer unit-cell is presented for designing a polarizer at 19 GHz for satellite applications in the Ka band. A periodic arrangement of the proposed unit cell converts linearly polarized incident fields into a circularly polarized LHCP or RHCP fields. The element is based on a gridded Jerusalem cross which achieves a full transmission phase difference between the two orthogonal polarizations. The maximum insertion loss is 0.4 dB in the band of 18.2-20.2 GHz. The 3dB axial ratio bandwidth is 15%. The full-wave analysis of HFSS validates the performance characteristics of the proposed polarizer unit cell.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Networks-Based Sea Ice Detection From TDS-1 Data
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a convolutional neural networks (CNNs)-based scheme for sea ice detection from TechDemoSat1 (TDS-1) delay-Doppler maps (DDMs). DDM images were employed as input and SIC data from passive microwave sensors were modified as targeted output. Two different CNNs were designed and tested with the full-size DDM data (128-by-20 pixels) and the further processed ones (40-by-20 pixels, and with fixed position in each image). The performance was also compared with the existing neural networks (NNs)-based method. It was found that when DDM data are adequately preprocessed CNNs and NNs share similar accuracy, otherwise the former outperforms the latter. Further conclusion was thus drawn that CNNs were more tolerant to the data format changes than NNs.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Effect of Roughness of 3D Printed Structure on Performance of Microwave Devices
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, 3D printed X band waveguide are proposed with epoxy coating as the conductor. Since the 3D printed structures end up having rough surfaces due to laying separate layers of the melted plastic on top of each other, this phenomena should be also considered in the simulation model. The roughness of the surface depends on the printing tip dimensions and the printing conditions. The whole structure is printed with a 3D printer and then is dipped into a low viscosity conductive solution to form the conductive layer on the inner walls of the waveguide. The waveguide system then is fed using coaxial cables. The results show the roughness can influence the transmission loss especially if the conductivity of the coated conductor layer is not as high as the conventional waveguide.

articleTitle: A Wearable Radiometric Antenna for Non-Invasive Brain Temperature Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband cavity backed antenna for continuous brain temperature monitoring through passive microwave radiometry. The proposed antenna has a diameter of 20 mm and height of 4.56 mm operating between 2.723-5.032 GHz. The antenna structure consists of a triple slotted square patch with hexagonal shape that is matched to a human head phantom. The SAR analysis shows that the antenna is capable of receiving microwave energy from deep brain and as an enabling component, it is suitable for a wearable brain temperature sensing system.

articleTitle: New Tecnhique for IoT indoor localization by employing segmented UHF RFID bandwith using bandpass filters and circulators
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper proposes a new technique to extend the use of the UHF RFID technology in IoT localization-based applications. The technique is based on segmenting the bandwidth of the UHF RFID into smaller equal segments with the use of band pass filters and circulators. The system analysis performed using CST and signal flow graph derived equations.

articleTitle: A Compact Unidirectional Wideband Step Slot Antenna over an Artificial Magnetic Conductor
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A compact unidirectional wideband step slot antenna backed by a wideband artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) to work at the frequency band of 1.2-3.6 GHz is presented. The proposed AMC consists of two printed circuit board layers separated by an air gap including a10 $\times$10 cell periodic structure. A compact step slot antenna with overall dimensions of $0.27 \lambda_{L} \times 0.13 \lambda_{L} \times 0.001 \lambda_{L}$ is ($\lambda_{L}$ the free space wavelength of the lowest operating frequency) is placed over the 0 proposed AMC structure which acts as a wideband reflector. The designed antenna is fabricated and tested. The measured results show a unidirectional radiation pattern with the maximum gain of 8 dBi in the operating frequency band.

articleTitle: On False Radiation Enhancement of Small Antennas Coated with Materials and Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Incorrectly claimed radiation enhancement of antennas using material and metamaterial coating is revisited. The antenna is represented by a coated spherical dipole, and its exact electromagnetic problem is solved analytically, in terms of spherical wave functions. Then, it is excited by a practical voltage source and the resulting antenna aperture voltage is determined using the equivalent circuit model of the source and the antenna, in terms of the source internal and antenna input impedances. It is shown that the coating parameters affect the antenna input impedance significantly, which causes dramatic changes on the antenna excitation voltage. In particular, at resonance of the modes inside the coating the antenna input impedance approaches zero, and the antenna aperture excitation diminishes accordingly. This dramatic variation of the antenna excitation voltage compensates for the perceived enhancement of the antenna radiation power due to the coating resonances. Consequently, the antenna radiation power remains finite and well behaved.

articleTitle: An Efficient and Compact Wireless Solution for Blood Sterilization Apparatus
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Advancements in the medical industry are some of the key contributions of the scientific community. One related direction of research is the X-ray sterilization of blood that is stored for future use. Currently, the tags used to indicate the irradiation level of the blood rely on visual indicators rather than an automated method. As a result, the irradiation levels of the blood cannot be ascertained. This paper proposes a new wireless dosimeter tag to measure the radiation levels with sufficient precision so as to avoid any material wastage and costs. The tag relies on an RF tag which consists of a CMOS transmitter, energy harvesting component and an off-chip inkjet printed antenna. In this paper, using 0.13 μm CMOS technology a floating gate MOSFET dosimeter design and an off-chip inkjet printed antenna are presented. These two components are the basic building blocks of the complete wireless dosimeter system. The floating gate MOSFET design is studied for its pre and post-radiation performance. The measured results show how the difference in the device current can be used for the radiation dose measurements. For the antenna, a printed antenna with suitable shielding is employed to enhance its radiation performance in the dissipative blood environment. The measured radiation pattern shows adequate gain and back-lobe radiation characteristics, thus making the surroundings invisible to the antenna and best suited for the intended application.

articleTitle: Millimiterwave (5G) Broadband Compact Slot Antenna for the Automotive Shark-fin Mobile and 5G Mobile Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The main goal of this paper is to declare a novel compact antenna with wideband characteristics at 28 GHz, with the aim of using in the 5G mobile networks and shark-fin mobile systems. The antenna dimensions and parameters are optimized over simulation and measurement to give better results. Measurements verified the response of antenna at the operating 5G frequency band (28 GHz). The proposed antenna attains a measured gain of 7.1 dB at 28 GHz. The measured impedance bandwidth is also about 20% at MMW operating band.

articleTitle: Groove Gap wave guide Slot Array Antenna in Millimeter Wave Band
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a millimeter-wave wave guide slot array antenna based on groove gap wave guide (GGW) technology is proposed. It has been shown that GGW is an appropriate alternative for the conventional rectangular wave guide in the millimeter wave range since there is no need for electrical contacts between metal parts to confine the field to the propagating channel. The proposed antenna provides the fractional bandwidth of 4.5% and maximum gain of 14.4 dBi at the operating frequency.

articleTitle: Wideband Matching of a Coaxial Waveguide Feed Using an Iris Matching Network
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: We are designing ultra-wideband feed antennas for radio astronomy using nested coaxial waveguide horns. A limitation of coaxial waveguide horns is their poor matching to free space, and thus high reflection coefficient. In this work, we use an iris matching network to improve the aperture mismatch over a wide range of frequency. A design methodology for iris matching networks is presented and used to study bandwidth and matching tradeoffs. We present a 2-iris matching network design that reduces the overall reflection coefficient from -6.5 dB to -13 dB over a 2:1 bandwidth ratio.

articleTitle: Overview of Single Conductor Power Transfer With Open-Ended Helical Resonators
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)

authors.preferredName: Susanna Vital de Campos de Freitas

abstract: This paper explores the operation of a single conductor power transfer (SCPT) system, utilizing two open-ended helical resonators. Contactless power transfer is established over a metallic structure by means of coils to couple energy to the resonators and to the load. The operation of the SCPT system is analyzed based on an analogy with conventional resonant inductive power transfer with two pairs of coils-resonators. Finally, two other methods for SCPT with helical resonators are outlined for comparison purposes.

articleTitle: Series Expansions for Matrix Inverses
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Various convergent matrix series formulae for the inverse of positive definite matrices are derived starting from series expansions of a simple matrix exponential function. The structure of these series assures a stable numerical computation since successive terms of the series are obtained through a multiplication with a matrix whose condition becomes better and better as the computation progresses.

articleTitle: Triband Impedance Transformer for Frequency Dependent Complex Load
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A TBIT (triband impedance transformer) for matching a FDCL (frequency dependent complex load) is proposed. The proposed design is composed of a DBIT (dual-band) and a DTBIT (dual-to-triband impedance transformer). The design takes advantage of available equations to obtain the transformer parameters values. The design is validated via simulations and measurements with matching achieved at GSM900, GSM1800 and 2.4 GHz ISM band.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of a Conical Horn Antenna using Converging Lenses in Line-of-sight Millimeter-wave Links
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, the performance of a conical horn antenna combined with converging lenses, over a 60 GHz millimeter-wave line-of-sight (LOS) wireless link, is experimentally investigated. In this context, the transformation optics concept is employed by placing plano-convex (PCX) and bi-convex (BCX) lenses a short distance from the aperture of a transmitting antenna in order to boost the gain and, accordingly, the overall dynamic range of the system. In fact, an increase in the received power of approximately 7.3 dB with the PCX lens is achieved, whereas the BCX lens has increased the received power of about 14.7 dB, compared to the reference case in which both lenses have not been employed.

articleTitle: Dual-Beam Leaky-Wave Antenna Based on Substrate Integrated Printed Ridge Gap Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A dual-beam leaky-wave antenna (LWA) based on the printed ridge gap waveguide (PRGW) technology is presented. A new H-polarized 1D-periodic substrate integrated gap waveguide leaky-wave antenna (SIGW-LWA) is designed, which has good scanning in backward and forward quadrant simultaneously. A dual-beam radiation pattern is achieved due to simultaneous excitation of two space harmonics (β<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sub> and β<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sub>). The beams scanning range for the proposed antenna started from -67° to -35° for the proper wave and 16° to 28° for the improper wave. The peak gains of the antenna for the proper and improper waves are 17.4 dBi and 16.2 dBi, respectively, with less than 1.3 dBi variation in both quadrants. The proposed antenna has wide impedance bandwidth and narrow fan beams through the whole operating frequency band of 59-67 GHz.

articleTitle: V-band Printed Ridge Gap Waveguide Phased Array Antenna with ±40° Scanning Angular Sector and ETSI Class II Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: We present a multilayer printed ridge gap waveguide (PRGW) phased array antenna based on Rotman Lens (RL) beam forming network for V-band sensing applications. It employs PRGW Rotman Lens as a beam switching network to design multi-beam antenna. Both phase shift network (PSN) and BFN will be made in printed circuit board in multi-layer platform based on PRGW technology. A prototype phased-array system is designed with eleven beam ports and sixteen array ports. The simulated results validated PGW design, and ± 40¼ scanning angular sector capability. The beam ports radiation patterns for both E-and H-planes satisfy intended ETSI class II standard side lobe envelope with side lobe levels lower than -12dB and wide impedance bandwidth over operating band.

articleTitle: Anti-Jamming GNSS Antenna for Timing Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a global navigation satellite system (GNSS) circularly polarized ceramic patch antenna using the Yagi-Uda theory to generate a null in the right hand circular (RHC) gain pattern at the horizon and around all azimuth angles to mitigate ground-based interference. The study shows that you can control the nulling elevation angle by changing the spacing of the directors used in this Yagi structure. The optimized results show an important attenuation of the RHC gain at an elevation of 15 degrees. At this elevation the RHC gain is 35 dB down from the max gain which is close to 8 dBic at zenith. The proposed AJ3000 antenna is an efficient and low-cost solution to reduce the impact of intentional and unintentional interference in the higher GNSS band for timing applications.

articleTitle: Modeling of Dielectric Resonator Filter for Multiplexer Design
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid model of a dielectric resonator (DR) Ku-band filter is presented. The model is developed to accurately simulate the DR filter's response over a wide frequency range for applications in multiplexer design. The hybrid model contains a neural network (NN) model in combination with a circuit model. To ensure the accuracy and improve the efficiency, the NN model is based on a simplified structure of the output iris of a DR filter. The circuit model represents the rest of the DR filter. A good agreement is observed between the hybrid model and EM simulation results.

articleTitle: A Dynamically Balanced OpenMP-CUDA Implementation of PDE-Based Contrast Source Inversion for Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: An implementation of a PDE-based Contrast Source Inversion (CSI) algorithm using a hybrid Open MP-CUDA parallel programming model is presented for the acceleration of microwave imaging. The CSI algorithm uses a time-harmonic discontinuous Galerkin method forward solver. The programming model ensures high computational throughput by dynamically balancing the amount of work performed on the GPU and CPU. The resulting implementation is capable of substantial speed-up, bringing the computational performance to near real-time. Implementation and optimization details are discussed; results show GPU acceleration alone gives a speedup of at least 5 times.

articleTitle: The Shaping of Decoupling Surfaces for Microstrip Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Decreasing the mutual coupling between the beamports of a multi-antenna system is an important task in MIMO wireless communications work and some other applications. Decoupling surfaces are often used for such purposes. This paper shows how shape optimization of such surfaces may be used to provide the coupling reduction needed.

articleTitle: Temperature Impact on Resonant Frequency of Rectangular Microstrip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A theoretical prediction of resonant frequency temperature behavior of rectangular microstrip patch antenna (MPA) fundamental mode is mathematically formulated in this paper. Knowledge of frequency drift due to temperature is of crucial importance for narrow banded MPA especially in harsh environment applications. In this paper, we demonstrate that by an adequate selection of substrate material frequency drift can be greatly reduced. Mathematical formulation of frequency drift reveals impact of patch width to substrate thickness ratio as well as substrate thickness on frequency stability. Among all commercially available substrates the antennas modeled on Rogers TMM10, TMM10i and Rogers RO3035 exhibit the best resonance temperature behavior, giving frequency drift between 1 ppm/°C and 6 ppm/°C.

articleTitle: On the Enhancement of Surface Plasmon Resonance Biosensors by Graphene for Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Since the introduction of fiber optic technology to Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) sensor design, Fiber Optic SPR (FO-SPR) sensors became more practical and adaptable for in situ remote sensing compared to previous prism based SPR sensors. Due to this evolution is SPR sensors, there has been a surge in interest in further integrating and enhancing these sensors for various in situ medical diagnostics applications and Graphene has emerged as a promising candidate to facilitate the enhancement of the sensitivity and lifetime of these sensors. In this paper we show the main performance parameters of SPR sensors, propose an analysis model and discuss recent work on Graphene enhanced SPR sensors.

articleTitle: An Invariant Dual-beam Snowflake Antenna for Future 5G Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A broadband snowflake antenna for future 5G and millimeter-wave communications is presented. The proposed antenna has a size of 8 × 5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The antenna consists of a central hexagon surrounded by a series of symmetrically placed smaller hexagons around it, resulting in broadband characteristics. The impedance bandwidth of the proposed antenna ranges from 25.284-29.252 GHz. The antenna has a gain of 3.12 dBi at 28 GHz and is more than 98% efficient. A distinct feature of the proposed antenna is its dual-beam radiation pattern. The two beams remain fixed at ±50° even if the frequency is varied with in its operating band. The proposed antenna is modelled on thin Rogers substrate which makes it very useful for future 5G smart phones.

articleTitle: MEMS Based Reconfigurable Superconducting Bandstop Filters
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: An architecture for a reconfigurable MEMS based bandstop filter is presented. The architecture is comprised of a circulator and bandpass filters with embedded switches required to cycle through the allowable tuning states. The integration of MEMS switches and high temperature superconductors is proposed to realize high Q, low loss structures. A single switched channel bandstop filter and a three channel, 8 state bandstop filter implementing a reconfigurable manifold coupled switched multiplexer are both presented with a combination of measured and simulated circuits to validate the proposed filtering architecture.

articleTitle: 1-bit Linearly Polarized Unit-Cell for Transmitarray Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a unit-cell for transmitarray antenna working at X-band is presented. The unit-cell is designed to provide 1-bit phase quantization at 12 GHz according to ON/OFF state of switches. The unit-cell is based on a multi-layer structure with a combination of a C-patch and a ring slot loaded by a rectangular gap. The simulation results show that the unit-cell can provide two values of transmission phase with a step of 180° at 12 GHz. A transmitarray antenna is also simulated to verify the performance of the unit cells. Simulated results show a good radiation pattern and validate the beam-switching capability.

articleTitle: Research on Antennas for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, an overview of some of the research activities in the Applied Electro-Magnetics Engineering Laboratory (AEMEL) are summarized. The major topics presented here are related to our research on antennas for biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Probe-fed Rectangular Flat-wire Open Loop Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Although both round and rectangular wires can be used to construct loop antennas, the rectangular wires, especially the ones with high aspect ratios, are much more efficient than the round ones with the same physical cross-sectional area. In this work, a probe-fed rectangular flat-wire open loop antenna is investigated. Simulations on different antenna parameters is conducted. The simulation results demonstrate that the sensitivity of the resonant frequency to different parameters varies, and two of the most sensitive parameters are the loop width and the air gap between the loop and the ground. These two parameters are also capable of modifying the miniaturization capability of such antennas. Interestingly, increasing the loop width can miniaturize the antenna without degrading the antenna performance. Instead, it can increase the efficiency and the gain of the antenna. This study was finally verified by good agreement between the simulation and measurement results of a fabricated antenna.

articleTitle: Miniaturized CPW Rat-Race Coupler Using the Superformula
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a new design of a CPW rat race coupler at 1.8 GHz that employs the superformula to draw the shape of the coupler. The meander-shape like circumference of the coupler allows for around 83% reduction in the size of the coupler as compared with circular conventional coupler. Simulated results for the magnitude and phase of the S-parameters are provided using HFSS with good results.

articleTitle: 60-GHz Circularly Polarized Annular Patch Antenna Fed by Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A low-profile circularly polarized (CP) slot-coupled microstrip annular patch antenna (MPA) excited by substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) is suggested as a building block for large-scale phased arrays used in various millimeter wave wireless technologies. L-shaped slot is used to excite two orthogonal modes of the patch with equal amplitude and 90 degree phase difference. The antenna structure is simulated by the Full-wave EM solver from ANSYS. The antenna exhibits wide impedance bandwidth (reflection coefficient less than -10 dB) of 57-65 GHz and axial ratio (AR) of less than 3dB in the range of 56-61.7 GHz.

articleTitle: New Series Formulae for Computing Accurately Matrix Exponentials
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The matrix series formulae presented for the computation of the matrix exponential can be applied to general matrices, positive definite or not, of arbitrary condition. Their main feature consists in the fact that each new term of the infinite series involved is computed by the multiplication of the previous term with a matrix which is better and better conditioned, tending to the identity matrix, and therefore allowing a stable and accurate numerical computation.

articleTitle: Proof of Concept Low-Loss Reconfigurable Reflectarray for Beam Steering
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a low-loss reconfigurable reflectarray (RA) design in the X-Band. It has been observed in the literature that the majority of the reconfigurable RAs are operating at the lower frequency bands (less than 5 GHz). This work is based on stretching the string towards the higher frequency bands and observing the performance of reconfigurable RAs in various aspects. An X-Band low-loss, and compact reconfigurable RA is investigated. A varactor loaded aperture coupled element is used to achieve the phase tuning agility. The element is designed by dividing the transmission line (TL) into two parts, and electronically connecting them through a single surface mount Hyper abrupt varactor diode. The proposed element exhibits 265° dynamic phase tuning ability. The element is a square of length 15.6mm (0.6 × λ at 10.5 GHz). A biasing network is also designed to isolate the RF signal from the DC. An equivalent circuit model is verified with the full-wave analysis. A reconfigurable RA of 3 × 3 elements is designed, and its ability to ±45° dynamic beam steering is evaluated for center-fed and offset feeding method. The proposed RA exhibits good potential in electronically steering the beam within ±40° with a scan loss of 4.5 dBi (from broadside), with both feed method (@ 10.5 GHz).

articleTitle: Maxwellian Fields and Geometry, Field Behaviour Near Region Boundaries and Sharp Discontinuities – a Review
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The solution of Maxwell's equation is normally determined subject to boundary conditions, and conducting boundaries have the most influence on the field behaviors, especially near sharp discontinuities, where the transverse field components become singular. It is shown that if the region outside the boundary with curvature discontinuities is mapped onto a region with a smooth boundary the reciprocal of the metric coefficient of the transformation describes exactly the singular behavior of the field components near the surface discontinuities. This is shown first mathematically for a conducting wedge. Then, the problem of a TM scattering by the wedge and a conducting prism is investigated, and shown again the same relationship between the surface currents and the reciprocal of the transformation metric coefficients. This property is used to develop a new integral equation by eliminating the singularity of the surface current in the integral equation. This study also showed that the product of the prism surface current and the metric coefficient of the transformation behaved nearly the same as the surface current on a corresponding circular cylinder, an interesting geometrical relationship.

articleTitle: Phase Analysis of a Semi-Passive RFID Indoor Localization System
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A full electromagnetic simulation model for a novel indoor localization system of a semi-passive radio frequency identification (RFID) tag is presented. The method is based on the phase of the backscattered wave collected by an antenna array attached to the RFID reader. Results demonstrate that the proposed simulation model comparatively provides an accurate estimation as well as assessment tool of phase measurements for indoor localization application. In addition, effects of the mutual coupling of the antenna array elements on the phase measurements found to be negligible due to the robustness of the proposed system.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Dual-Band Tunable AMC Structure for GNSS Antennas and Its Performance Trade-Offs
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A novel low-profile dual-band tunable artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) structure based on the choke ring is presented in this paper. The structure is tuned to the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) frequencies of L2 (1227.60 MHz) and L1 (1575.42 MHz). Using full-wave simulations for the Dorne & Margolin (DM) antenna mounted on the AMC structure, it is demonstrated that the proposed dual-band structure provides good multipath performance at both L2 and L1. Compared to the conventional choke ring, the novel design provides a 52% reduction in height and a 26% reduction in diameter.

articleTitle: FM antenna with soft visual impact made from micrometric mesh metal technology
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: An optically transparent and electrically small FM radio receiving antenna has been designed and fabricated from a micrometric mesh silver layer printed onto a glass substrate. The studied FM antenna consists of a transparent meandering monopole associated with a micrometric size MESFET transistor. A sheet resistance lower than 0.22Ω/sq and an optical transparency of 87 % in the visible light spectrum are obtained. The Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) and the Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) are both measured, compared with those of a commercial monopole antenna, and discussed.

articleTitle: A Broad-band Transition Between a Silicon Waveguide and a CPWG at W-band
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a novel broad-band silicon waveguide based transition at W-band. The proposed transition from a CPWG line to a silicon image waveguide demonstrates the insertion loss of better than 0.65 dB within the range of 85-110 GHz. The silicon image waveguide location is fixed by two sets of legs for increasing the mechanical stability and reducing the alignment challenges.

articleTitle: Supporting Advanced Breast Imaging Research Through Reconfigurable Numerical Breast Models
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents development of reconfigurable numerical breast models to support advanced breast imaging research. These features are realized through application of a 3D modelling method to 3T magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans. The reconfigurable model features are discussed in the context of supporting both initial and advanced development stages of emerging microwave breast imaging technologies. Further, these features are demonstrated through sample model reconstructions.

articleTitle: Digital Implementation of a Beam Control Scheme in Phased Array for Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: An efficient and standard-compliant hardware and software architecture for the digital control part of active phased arrays is proposed in this paper. The FPGA-based proposed scheme is designed to meet the requirements of the receiver side of the ground station in mobile satellite communication systems. The digital control part has been implemented on Artix-7 and ZYNQ-7000 FPGAs. Both simulation and measurement results prove the capability of the proposed structure for mobile satellite systems.

articleTitle: Recyclable Materials as a Means of Electromagnetic Shielding
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Currently, shielding effectiveness represents a fundamental property of materials designed to resist electromagnetic fields effect. There are many materials suitable for shielding; however, the authors decided to use recyclable plastic materials whose surface was provided with gold or carbon nano-layer. The experiment aimed at determining the influence of conductive material nano-layers and application to commercially available security products.

articleTitle: High Gain High Dense Dielectric Patch Antenna Using FSS Superstrate for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: High gain low profile linearly polarized square dense dielectric (DD) patch antenna using a frequency selective surface (FSS) superstrate layer is proposed. The implemented antenna is designed, and excited by aperture coupled feeding technique. The DD patch is used as a radiated element. An array of frequency selective surface FSS is used to enhance the gain of the antenna. The antenna gain is enhanced by 10 dBi. The implemented antenna obtained a gain of about 17.78 dBi at 28 GHz with radiation efficiency of 90 %. Furthermore, it has a bandwidth of about 9 %. It has a good radiation performance. For some attractive advantages such as low profile, low cost, light weight, small size, and ease of implementation, the proposed antenna is a good candidate for millimeter wave wireless communications.

articleTitle: On the Significance of Periodic Structures in Applied Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Periodic structures have played a key role in applied electromagnetics in different contexts such as frequency selective surfaces, phased arrays. Relative size of the lattice periodicity as compared to operating wavelength has a strong bearing on the functionality of these structures. In other words, the functionality constrains the lattice size (also referred to as periodicity or cell size). Different ranges of periodicity lead to fundamentally different types of operation on the part of the periodic structure. Three examples will be discussed in this paper to further illustrate the impact of cell size on the response of the periodic structure. The first example will address the realization of a volume hologram using artificial dielectric technology which necessitates a 3D lattice size much smaller than the operating wavelength. A multi-band hybrid reflector-reflectarray configuration with a dedicated radiation signature at each band will be discussed next as an illustration of a periodic structure with a cell size of the same order as the operating wavelength. Finally, realization of a beam combiner using a Talbot grating will be presented as an example of a periodic structure that utilizes periodicity in excess of the operating wavelength.

articleTitle: Design and Test of a Dual-Frequency Dual-Polarization Microstrip Patch Array Prototype
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: We present aspects in the design and test of a dualfrequency, dual-polarization microstrip antenna array, which operates in both L-band and X-band. The antenna is proposed for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) applications that require low weight, low profile, and compact designs. The prototype antenna unit cell consists of a single dual-polarized perforated L-band patch, with 36 dual-polarized X-band patches integrated into the same planar geometry. We present design concepts, simulation results, and measurement results for the fabricated prototype.

articleTitle: On the Error Study of Surface-Volume-Surface EFIE for solving the 3-D Scattering Problems on Composite Dielectric Objects
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Recently proposed Surface-Volume-Surface Electric Field Integral Equation (SVS-EFIE) has been studied for the 3D scattering problems on homogeneous and composite dielectric objects. Compared to traditional surface integral equations, the SVS-EFIE has only electric-field-type of Green's function which reduces the number of unknowns in half. In order to validate the accuracy of the SVS-EFIE for composite objects, its solution is compared against the solution of FEKO commercial solver and the behavior of the error is studied at the junctions of a NASA almond composite structure.

articleTitle: A Contrast Source Inversion Method for Multiple Inhomogeneous Backgrounds
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The Contrast Source Inversion (CSI) method has been successfully applied to inverse problems in electromagnetics for a number of applications. Forward solvers supporting inhomogeneous backgrounds provide a means to incorporate prior information into the inversion process, and are a continued focus of research for improving imaging results. To expand the capabilities of CSI for exploiting physical and/or numerical backgrounds, we present a CSI formulation that supports multiple simultaneous inhomogeneous backgrounds.

articleTitle: Beamwidth Effects on Laser RCS of Partially Convex Objects in Random Media for E-Wave Polarization
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate effects of beamwidth on the laser radar cross-section (LRCS) of objects with different complexities in random media. We assume concave illumination region and consider a random medium such as turbulence with various coherence lengths. Horizontal incident wave polarization (E-wave incidence) is postulated.

articleTitle: Solution Convergence in Exterior Electromagnetic Boundary Value Problems and Its Dependence on the Numerical Methods-a Review
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In numerical solution of electromagnetic problems, boundary conditions play an essential role to ensure the uniqueness of the solution. The problem may be solved by a variety of methods, such as the integral or differential equation methods, a modal expansion method, or some random application of boundary conditions on the object. In any case, the application of boundary conditions is used to determine the unknown field quantity of the formulation to be used for determining the entire solution in the desired space. The convergence of the solution, therefore, depends on the selection of the unknown and the method used for its determination. However, in exterior boundary value problems the field quantities of interest are at far distances from the boundaries, where the field behaviors are dependent on the entire boundary of the object. Thus, the behaviour of the far field vectors is different from those on the boundary. This problem is investigated here by means of simple scattering by conducting objects having simple, as well as, complex shapes. It is shown that, while the convergence of the solution for determining the boundary fields can be slow, or difficult to obtain, depending on the shape of the object, the convergence of the far field solution is usually more rapid. In particular, the convergence of the far field is mostly dependent on the size of the object, rather than its shape.

articleTitle: Long-Range Surface Plasmon Lasers
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: We review work on integrated optical components operating with long-range surface plasmons, particularly active structures incorporating an optical gain medium for use as surface plasmon amplifiers and lasers.

articleTitle: Enhanced Design of Reconfigurable Integrated Filter and Antenna Based on Multilayer Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, an enhancement design of reconfigurable integrated SIW and patch antenna using the varactor diodes is presented. To realize the concept, reconfigurable SIW filter and reconfigurable patch antenna were combined using the multilayer technique into a single structure. To validate the design technique, the equivalent circuit model of the tunable varactor diode network is presented to study the tunability mechanism. The experimental performance shows good agreement with the tunable attenuation response up to 15.5 dB, better than 10 dB in the passband region. The investigation presented here may facilitate improvements in an integrated technique with a good tuning capability for wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Analysis of Coupling and Loading in RF Coils for Magnetic-Resonance Imaging
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this contribution generalized field-theoretical and circuit-based analyses of field distribution and element coupling and loading in MRI-RF coils are presented and/or revisited. They are applicable to high-field operations, in which the geometrical dimensions of the coil become comparable to the Larmor wave-length. The circuit-based analysis utilizes the characteristic properties of circulant matrices that describe periodic structures with ring-type coupling. It allows for controlling the coupling without the need of minimizing or eliminating it. It also gives useful equations for the calculation of the coil loading, which is needed for the optimization of its operation in both transmitting and receiving scenarios. The paper is essentially of a fundamental nature and presents and/or revisits physical insights and useful equations. Therefore, no simulation or measurement results are included.

articleTitle: On the Number of Degrees of Freedom in Dual-Polarized GNSS Adaptive Arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: It is known that a dual-polarized adaptive array with N elements has a maximum of 2N-1 degrees of freedom for beamforming. For small global navigation satellite system (GNSS) adaptive arrays, we show that this maximum can be easily achieved if the interferer polarizations are random. For the case of right-hand circularly-polarized (RHCP) interferers however, we show that the maximum degrees of freedom can only be achieved if the element patterns are asymmetric in the principal E- and H-planes.

articleTitle: V-band Multi-port Waveguide Direct-Conversion Receiver: Design and M-ary PSK Demodulation Results
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper proposes an experimental validation of 60-GHz short-range wireless link using a robust multi-port direct conversion receiver based on waveguide technology. The employed multi-port waveguide structure is manufactured using brass material to achieve an excellent electrical conductivity and high corrosion resistance. The performances of direct conversion receiver based on the fabricated multi-port structure are experimentally demonstrated in terms of various M-ary PSK modulated signals (BPSK, QPSK, 8PSK, and 16 PSK) through a reliable test bench setup. The obtained results demonstrate the ability of the proposed multi-port receiver to accurately handle low-power input signals, while performing various direct M-ary PSK demodulation at 60 GHz millimeter-wave band. Moreover, the robustness, the higher corrosion and wear resistance of the fabricated multi-port structure make it a highly suitable for use in challenging outdoor environments, such as future V-band inter-building wireless links.

articleTitle: Equivalent circuit for an ultra-wide bande monopole antenna inserted in a magneto-dielectric medium
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: An equivalent circuit for a wide-band monopole antenna inserted in an infinite lossless Magneto-Dielectric Medium (MDM) has been developed, from its equivalent circuit in the air which consists of N RLC parallels. The equivalent circuit is sufficiently accurate for a broadband simulation comparing the simulated data obtained from a full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: The Use of 3-D Printing in Teaching MEMS Device Design and Fabrication
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents an overview of how three-dimensional (3-D) printing can be used as an educational tool in the area of Micro-Electromechanical Systems (MEMS) and microfabrication. Microfabrication processes used to realize MEMS devices typically take place in a cleanroom. The use of 3-D printing to emulate the process of MEMS device layout, fabrication and design provides a cost-effective alternative method to teaching MEMS fabrication and modeling without the need to access a cleanroom.

articleTitle: Excitation of Hyperbolic Plasmons and Transition Radiation in Phosphorene by a Swift Electron
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: We analyze the energy loss channels for a fast electron traversing a monolayer phosphorene under oblique incidence taking the retardation effects into account.

articleTitle: Extraction of Sea Ice Information from SAR for Numerical Sea Ice Prediction
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: New techniques for automated extraction of sea ice information from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) RADARSAT-2 images with a very high level of confidence are presented. The ice/water detection approach developed based on more than 15,000 SAR images (2010-2016) and corresponding Canadian Ice Service (CIS) Image Analysis products is able to classify 65.4% of SAR data with the accuracy of 99.8%. Introduction of an auxiliary SAR image acquired several hours before allowed to further increase the number of retrievals. Ice concentration is also estimated based on the number of ice/water retrievals. The large number of SAR retrievals with very high accuracy makes it possible to assimilate them in operational Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) Regional Ice-Ocean Prediction System (RIOPS).

articleTitle: Wideband Unit-Cell Design For X-band Transmitarray
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents in detail the design of a wideband unit-cell for X-band passive transmitarray. The unit-cell is based on multi-layer structure and consists of four conducting layers printed on two identical substrates. A set of eight unit-cells are optimized to cover full 360° phase range and to obtain eight transmission phase states with a step of 45° for a common -3 dB bandwidth of 2.0 GHz. To evaluate the performance of the proposed unit-cell, a transmitarray antenna is designed and simulated at X-band. The simulated results show that the transmitarray provides maximum gain of 23.6 dBi, corresponding to a high aperture efficiency of 38.0%.

articleTitle: Wideband Circular Polarized Antenna for Satellite Based Navigation Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper we propose a wideband antenna structure to cover the non-military satellite navigation frequency spectrum. The antenna structure consists cross dipole elements fed with 90° phase difference to provide proper axial ratio within the whole frequency band. The axial ratio is improved by using two parasitic elements near to each dipole arm. The dipole arms are designed on a FR4 substrate and placed above a ground plane to reduce the effect of any metallic object behind the antenna. The impedance matching is better than -15 dB in 1-1.7 GHz and axial ratio is better than 3 dB in 1.17-1.67 GHz, covering the required bandwidth for satellite navigation systems.

articleTitle: The dispersion and damping of the Dirac plasmon polariton of graphene in water
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: We study theoretically the dispersion and damping of the Dirac plasmon polariton in graphene in the range of frequencies from the microwave to the near infrared in the presence of a thick layer of pure water at room temperature.

articleTitle: Adjoint-Based Design of a Crossed-Ellipse Absent THz Filter
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this work, we propose a crossed-ellipse metal mesh THz filters on thick substrates. These filters exploit the trapped-mode excitation via inserting a smaller crossed ellipse centered with the outer absent one. An optimization approach to control the bandwidth of metal mesh THz filters is presented. Adjoint sensitivity analysis is utilized to provide the derivatives of the objective function for the optimizer. EM simulations are carried out to illustrate the efficiency of the technique in varying the filter's bandwidth about a certain operating frequency of 300 GHz.

articleTitle: Wrapped Resistively Loaded Bow-tie Antenna for Use in UAV Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The wrapped resistively loaded bow-tie antenna (WRLBA) is proposed for UAV applications in this paper. The pulse radiating characteristics such as antenna reflection in freespace and reflected waveform from target are simulated and analyzed. The calculated fidelity factor for wrapped bow-ie antenna (WBA) and WRLBA are 0.80 and 0.88, respectively, which are suitable for sensing applications.

articleTitle: Flexible Antenna on Drone Arms for Near-field Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper proposes the wrapped antenna designed by flexible substrate for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) applications. The proposed flexible wrapped resistively loaded bow-tie antenna (WRLBA) has simulated to evaluate the pulse radiating performance such as radiated waveform in time domain as a potential pulse radiating sensor. The simulated result is shown that the proposed WRLBA is very suitable for short pulse radiating applications.

articleTitle: Array Antenna Diagnosis from Far Field Data Using the Theory of Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a novel utilization of the theory of characteristic mode (TCM) is presented. We reconstruct the current distribution on an array of λ/2 dipole antenna from the known far-field pattern by employing TCM. The main goal of this work is accurate faults detection and calibration of large phased array antennas with low computational cost by using their far-field data. The proposed technique is based on decomposing the total radiating field into the orthogonal characteristic far-fields that are Linearly related to characteristic currents of the array antenna. By applying this method, the total current distribution on the antenna can be retrieved with an acceptable accuracy.

articleTitle: On the Validity of Standard and Accurate Local Surface Impedance Models
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Surface impedance models provide us with an efficient way of analyzing plasmonic circuits. The Standard and newly introduced accurate local surface impedance models, despite their usefulness and simplicity, cannot model the field variations when the dimensions of the structure are comparable to the penetration depth of the fields inside the object. In this paper, a validity criterion for these two models is introduced. Using this criterion will help choosing the appropriate approach to analyze plasmonic circuits and reduce the computational time and memory resources.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Metal-Only Dipole Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a new ultra-wideband metalonly dipole reflectarray (MODRA) antenna, designed to operate over the frequency range of 10-19 GHz. The proposed structure offers many advantages over the legacy design. For instance, its simplicity and lightweight enable us to develop a large-size reflectarray (RA) antenna, which can be deployed on any platform including a satellite. The proposed MODRA antenna consists of dipole antennas with varying lengths, which is mechanically supported by a rectangular metallic ring and a short-circuited metal strip. Stainless-steel metal has been suggested as the material to use to fabricate the proposed structure. Normal incident simulation shows that at 10 GHz the MODRA antenna realizes 339° phase range when the dipole lengths vary from 1mm to 14mm; furthermore, it realizes a 298° phase range at 19 GHz for the same dipole-length variation. The maximum reflection loss is found to be 0.51 dB and 0.2 dB at 10 GHz and 19 GHz, respectively. Finally, metal-only multi-dipole reflectarray (MOMDRA) antenna is employed as a simple solution to overcome the phase shift limitation of the MODRA antenna. Simulations show that reflection phases of 345° and 657° are realized at 10 GHz and 18 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Power Splitter Using Ridge Gap Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A reconfigurable wideband power splitter is designed using Ridge Gap Waveguide technology. The splitter depends on using a flat sheet between two RGWs and controlling the sheet deflection using a mechanism integrated in the pins regions where the electromagnetic fields are negligible. The splitter achieves a flat 3 dB power splitting from 14 GHz to 22 GHz when the sheet is not deflected. When a force acts on the sheet ends, the power split ratio may be changed with matching level better than 15 dB on the same band.

articleTitle: Random Auxiliary Sources Method based on Point Matching Versus RGW Testing
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A comparison between the Rao-Glisson-Wilton (RGW) testing and point matching on the performance of the Random Auxiliary Sources (RAS) method is introduced. The comparison includes the method accuracy, numerical stability as well as suitability for general purpose solutions including special treatments. The comparison includes a smooth spherical structure in addition to a structure with edges. The results show an advantage for point matching for a fat and smooth-surface structure and RGW testing for structures with edges, which is an indication of the general-purpose suitability of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Approximation of Multi Resonant Behaviour of Slotted Patch Antenna via Multi Cavity Model
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper an I shape patch antenna has been presented.. The epicenter of the research work is to justify the multi resonant behavior of a slotted patch antenna by setting a parallelism between the simulated results and the theoretical analysis performed by equating the slotted patch to multiple cavities. This theoretical analysis helps in anticipating the resonant frequencies for a given length and width of the slot that is to be made in the patch. The simulation of the antennas has been done using Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Microwave Studio V'14. The designs have also been fabricated and tested using Agilent's Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) E 5071 C series.

articleTitle: Development of a High Power Dielectric Antenna for Delivery of Picosecond Pulses
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Picosecond pulses can be used in electrostimulation for activating action potentials, promoting calcium release and affecting macromolecules. We report the development of a dielectric biconical antenna for delivery of picosecond pulses to target a tissue less than 2 cm in depth. For an antenna with a dielectric constant of 28, we obtained a maximum electric field of 1-2 kV/cm in water. This was for the input picosecond pulses of 50 kV. This field is about 6-10% of a field created by a parallel electrode gap energized with the same voltage. The antenna performance needs to be improved greatly to match the required field for electrostimulation. It was found that the dielectric material of the antenna is critical to the high voltage operation and needs to be carefully chosen and characterized.

articleTitle: 3-D Printed Flexible Heterogeneous Substrates with Customizable Gain and Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a 3-D printed flexible heterogeneous substrate for wearable antennas with customizable bandwidth and gain. These performance parameters are modified by varying the ratio of percentage area of Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS) to NinjaFlex. Five flexible 3-D printed mlcrostrlp patch antenna (MPA) prototypes are designed, realized and measured each with different percentage area ratios, where the MPA's RF performance is characterized with curvature. The live substrate designs are based on a combination of rigid ABS tiles of triangular shape surrounded with flexible NinjaFlex. All five designs show minimal antenna sensitivity to curvature, with a minimum resonant frequency shift of less than 1.2%. Results closely agree with simulations. Increasing the ABS area increases the MPA's gain, but reduces the bandwidth and increases substrate rigidity. This results in a highly customizable and cost-effective substrate that allows the antenna designer flexibility in the choice of design parameters.

articleTitle: A High-Gain Beam Steering Silicon Based Antenna Array for Sub-MmWave Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, we are presenting a low-cost and high-gain beam steering silicon-based antenna array for submmWave and THz applications, specifically for the next generation of 5G and radar systems. The antenna element is a parasitic tapered antenna for enhancing the gain while the size of the array is kept small. The beam steering happens by movement of a small metal sheet above each arm of the antenna array. The achieved gain of the system is 15.4 dBi at 86 GHz. The total scanning angle of 20 degrees is observed.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing of Oil Spills in Freezing Environments at the University of Manitoba Sea-ice Environmental Research Facility
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the research conducted to date at the University of Manitoba Sea-ice Environmental Research Facility pertaining to the microwave remote sensing of oil spills in the presence of sea ice. As such, a description of the facility and the design of oil-in-sea ice experiments is provided along with a summary of the primary findings of the research. Future plans to expand on work done with remote sensing of oil spills in freezing environments are also discussed.

articleTitle: Ka-band Antenna Array for Agile Frontends
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a Ka-band RF frontend tailored to digital beam forming. It consists of an antenna array realised in LTCC, which is connected to a soft substrate PCB containing the active components. The topology is suitable for various implementations of beamforming systems for applications, such as 5G mm-wave systems, IoT, and SatCom.

articleTitle: A Wideband Fully Planar Vivaldi Antenna for WPAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The availability of large bandwidth in the ISM band around 60 GHz is very useful for data hungry applications such as WPAN. Being allocated as an ISM band, several research papers have been published on completely integrated RF systems using CMOS technology. Although the circuits for these implementations have been realized on silicon, the antennas are usually done off-chip. The reason is the lossy nature of the silicon substrate for RF frequencies.
