Instead of using resonant antennas, if travelling wave antennas are used for such an application then a better efficiency can be achieved from such designs. In this work, a fully planar Vivaldi antenna is reported on 65 nm CMOS stack up. For the first time, the feed of the antenna is integrated on the same conductor layer as the antenna itself. Using this design technique the problem of thin gap between the metal layers have been mitigated. The final simulations show that the antenna covers the complete ISM band and works well from 57 GHz to 66 GHz. The gain of the antenna is -3dBi. The results show that the design is quite suitable for integration in a millimeter range transceiver for short range wireless communication.

articleTitle: Wide-beam circularly polarized curved wire antenna for millimetre wave application
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A wide-beam circularly polarized wire antenna with the beam-width of 162°, a uniform pattern, and an axial ratio of less than 2.3 dB over the whole beam-width is designed. This antenna is designed at 30 GHz as a sensing antenna for nearfield measurement and characterization of large phased array antennas.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a VHF Antenna Transparent to K-Band Satellite Communication Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A VHF blade antenna transparent to K-band frequencies (19 to 21 GHz) is proposed. In the K-band, the wave transmitted through the antenna undergoes a loss of less than 0.2 dB. The unit cells of the FSS constituting the VHF blade are made of meandre lines. The size of the cells at the VHF frequency is only Lx = Ly = 0. 0015λ, and they essentially behave as a solid conductor surface. The cell is printed an a thin flexible substrate that can be easily embedded in a radome.

articleTitle: Cryogenic L-band GaAs HEMT LNA for the Square Kilometer Array
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Cryogenic low noise amplifiers (LNAs) are in high demand for highly sensitive receivers for radio astronomy. This paper describes the design and testing of an extremely low noise amplifier based on 3-stage GaAs HEMTs and a microwave integrated circuit. Utilizing computer-aided design techniques, lumped passive components were adapted to integrate with GaAs low noise transistors to optimize the noise and return losses. This LNA design achieved an extremely low noise temperature of averaging only 1.3 K, having > 40 dB gain, and low input and output return losses <; -10 dB, in a wide bandwidth from 900 MHz to 2000 MHz at a physical temperature of 15 K. It realized high gain and an excellent gain stability of Allan variance <; 2×10- at cryogenic temperatures and meets the stringent requirements of the Square Kilometer Array receivers.

articleTitle: A Multi-Receiver Wireless Power Transfer System with Load Independence for Practical Wireless Charging Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Research and development of wireless power transfer have been intensified recently due to its potential to change the way we live and work. One of the technical challenges is to design a system whose output voltages are independent of loads since the loads represent different power receiving devices. Research work along this has been conducted; however, it has been focused on single-transmitter and single-receiver systems, while in practice, single-transmitter and multi-receiver systems are often seen and practical. In this paper, we analyze the multi-receiver systems and then propose a system with insertion of T-network; we drive the conditions for voltage independence of the loads. We run the simulations with Agilent ADS to verify the conditions and show the possibility of load independence for multi-receiver systems. The results are realistic and practical since ADS is a mature and widely acceptable simulator that have been proven experimentally and is considered to generate the results very close to reality. Therefore, the worked presented in this paper present the theoretical foundation and a starting point for designing practical multi-receiver wireless power transfer systems in the near future.

articleTitle: Modeling Radio Wave Scattering from Simple Rough, Layered Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The generalized function approach for modeling radio wave scattering has been used to develop expressions for the backscatter from rough surfaces and from horizontally stratified media. The research was initially used to model high frequency surface wave radar scattering from a rough ocean surface or across layers of ice covering the ocean. This paper extends the existing theory by assuming an arbitrary dielectric constant for a simple rough surface and by suggesting an approach to model the backscatter from a stratified medium that has a rough surface. When an arbitrary dielectric constant is used for the rough surface, the shape of the scattered field remains the same, but is weaker due to the transmission of energy through the surface. Scatter from rough surfaces and stratified media both can be expressed as the sum of a direct and reflected wave. This form is exploited to understand the scatter from a rough surface over layered media.

articleTitle: Plasmon Excitation and Transition Radiation in Graphene Traversed by a Fast Charged Particle
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A progress report is presented on recent theoretical investigations of the interaction of fast charged particles with single and multiple graphene layers. By adopting a fully relativistic formulation of the problem, special focus is placed on retardation effects in the energy loss of a charged particle due to electronic excitations in graphene, which include its plasmon polariton modes, as well as the energy that is emitted from graphene in the form of transition radiation. Using both empirical and ab initio models for the dynamic in-plane conductivity of graphene allows the exploration of energy losses at frequencies ranging from the terahertz to the ultraviolet.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis of Radiation Levels Allowed by International Standards in Conglomerate Wireless Systems in Different Urban Areas of the City of Guayaquil
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Today one of the most used methods in Telecommunications is the wireless technology, which uses electromagnetic waves to send or receive information. Due to the increase of these wireless systems and the nonionizing radiation that they can emit, the study of the impact that these radiations can have on the population is carried out constantly by the international organizations that watch over health. Because of this, international recommendations were created that are used by the State organisms to verify compliance with the limits of exposure to this type of radiation, how to measure them and methods of evaluating results. Therefore, this technical project is carried out with the objective of carrying out a comparative analysis of the levels of radiation permitted by international standards in the wireless systems in different urban areas of the city of Guayaquil.

articleTitle: New Wireless Power Transfer Systems Against Misalignments between Transmitters and Receivers
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) is the means that can cut the last wires in electronic wireless applications. Among the WPT technologies developed so far, magnetically coupled resonance (MCR) techniques have gained much attention to potentials for mid-range power transfers. However, misalignments between transmitters and receivers have become one of the major obstacles in improving the power transfer efficiency. This paper presents our recent progress in developing new MCR-WPT systems in mitigating the misalignment effects for wireless power transfers. Prototypes are developed and tested to demonstrate the effects of our proposed systems.

articleTitle: A Compact SIC Magic-T for W-band Phased Array Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents the conceptual design of a simple, compact and planar SIC magic-T structure based on the image substrate integrated dielectric (iSINRD) EM-periodic guide. Unlike conventional planar magic-Ts, the proposed magic-T does not require, metallic posts, slots or embedded dielectric phase shifters. It rather relies mainly on the boundary of the arms to achieve the typically high magic-T isolation. The frequency of operation is designed at 94 GHz.. Using Alumina dielectric (ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>=9.8), and with the E-arm being on the same plane as the H-arm, a very compact magic-T is conceived which makes it amenable for seamless integration of millimeter-wave circuits. The lateral dimensions of each arm are 0.41 × 0.64 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Perforation is done using square air-vias, each having a side length of 0.35 mm. The total size of the circuit is 4.41 × 4.67 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The 3-dB bandwidth of the proposed magic-T is ~1 GHz, centered at 94 GHz, and the return loss is better than 15 dB.

articleTitle: 60GHz optically transparent patch antenna arrays made of double-sided micrometric mesh metal layers
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The paper presents the performance of 60 GHz 4 × 2 transparent patch antenna arrays made of double-sided micrometric mesh metal layers. Optical transparency and microwave characteristics are studied and compared with those of an opaque array made of double-sided continuous metal layers. In particular, the influence of the mesh processing of the ground plane is investigated. The sheet resistance of the conducting layers remains below 0.5 Ω/sq associated with an average optical transparency close to 80% over the entire visible light spectrum.

articleTitle: From Computational Electromagnetics to mm-Wave Antennas: Influence of Lot Shafai
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, we review from personal perspective the influence of Lot Shafai on joint research on Computational Electromagnetics and Antenna Technology by partially retracing research activities over more than 35 years. The early joint research was on the development of analytical and numerical techniques for both direct and inverse scattering. Then our joint research activities have shifted toward antenna design.

articleTitle: Dielectric Resonator Antenna Fed by an Offset Tapered Microstrip Line
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents the investigation of a rectangular dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) fed by an offset tapered microstrip line. In the study, the width of the microstrip line and the width of the coupling area overlapping with the DRA on the side edge of the feed line are optimized so as to enhance the coupling and increase the impedance bandwidth. An -10dB S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> bandwidth of 11.3% around the centre frequency of 3.5GHz has been obtained in the experiment, compared to 3.4% using the centre feed. The antenna studied is aimed for applications in 5G communications at the 3.5GHz band.

articleTitle: Spectral and Temporal Dependence of the Nonlinear Refractive Index of Graphene for Use in Integrated Photonic Devices
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this work, we measure the nonlinear refractive index (n<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) of graphene using the Z-Scan technique as a function of varying spectral and temporal characteristics of the excitation laser. Recent works have worked to quantify the nonlinear index of refraction in graphene under various experimental conditions to only produce contradictory results. A laser source producing 100 fs pulses is tuned from 800-1050 nm and the n<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> is measured. Then the pulse is temporally expanded up to 500 fs using a prism pair stretcher at 900 nm and the n<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> is measured. The use of graphene in integrated nonlinear photonic devices such as alloptical modulators, warrants the characterisation of the nonlinear behaviour in graphene for device design. In addition to that, the study gave us insight into the physics of the ultrafast and large nonlinear response in graphene, showing agreement with our theoretical model.

articleTitle: Cavity Perturbation Technique to Characterize Dielectric Materials at Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The characterization of permittivity and dielectric loss of dielectric materials using a perturbation technique is conducted in simulation. The working frequency of this technique has been extended to the Ka-band. Simulation results demonstrate this perturbation technique is suitable for mm-wave characterization of high permittivity dielectric materials and maintains good accuracy.

articleTitle: Dual Input Interferometer Direct Conversion Receiver Architecture
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a dual input interferometer receiver front-end architecture for wireless point-to-point communications. The proposed front-end circuit is composed of two antennas and a passive junction of three couplers. This interferometer architecture enables direct demodulation of digital signals based on the same operation principle of six-port receivers (SPR). While the SPR theoretically exhibits 6dB power loss due to the nature of its passive junction, the proposed front-end only presents 3dB power loss. An experimental prototype has been designed and fabricated at center frequency of 5 GHz. Various PSK-QAM demodulations have been received with an average error vector magnitude (EVM) less than S.5%.

articleTitle: Multi-Port Push-Push Oscillator for Mutually Synchronized Oscillator Array
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A multi-port push-push oscillator using a slot ring resonator for oscillator array is proposed. In the oscillator array, the oscillators are mutually synchronized with adjacent oscillators via coupling circuits. Therefore, it is necessary that the oscillators have two ports for connecting the coupling circuits. The proposed oscillator has one port for the output signal that is the 2nd harmonic signal and two ports for the synchronization signals that are the fundamental signals. The output power of the 2nd harmonic signal is -9.95 dBm at 15.11 GHz and those of the fundamental signals for synchronization are -3.51 dBm and -5.16 dBm at 7.55 GHz.

articleTitle: Flexible Inspection Imaging System Based on MM-Wave SFCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents an imaging inspection system based on MM-wave stepped frequency continuous radar. The system structure is explained. The RF side of the system is tested successfully, and the experimental result is presented.

articleTitle: Implementation of Wideband Channel Modeling Based on Extended Kalman Filter Interpolation for MIMO-OFDM WLAN Channels
publicationTitle: 2018 18th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A new wideband simulation environments for multiple input-multiple output (MIMO) wide local area network (WLAN) channels is described, which covering several wireless communication services. Stimulated by the prerequisite of appropriate performance of link simulation techniques in study of communication systems are proposed in this paper. Specially, an algorithm is designated to estimate the fast-fading WLAN channels in high velocity vehicular in this paper. In order to adequately pursue channel response with fast time-varying, adaptive algorithm for channel estimation is essential. A tapped-delay line base-form is utilized for the multi-path channel, and a process with auto-regressive structure is applied for the time-correlation of the channel taps. The proposed algorithm is developed by an extended Kalman filter to estimate the amplitude and phase of channel frequency response. So, these parameters are achieved by applying known pilot symbols. It makes an efficient MIMO WLAN channel estimation from 2.4 to 4.8 GHz band for random antenna arrangements at the unknown transmitter and receiver. Finally, an experimental test is configured to verify the simulation results.
